title: Bitterroot Front 10 Year G-Z IRSC
description: 10/9/2026- Amendment 002 Posted. This Amendment provides responses to additional questions received and corrected solicitation documents. Past Performance evaluation criteria has been amended in the Solicitation to align with requested information in the instructions. Corrected documents are indicated with A002 in the file name with all changes indicated in red text. 9/17/2026- Amendment 001 Posted 8/3/2026- Replaces word versions of Attachements C04c_2a, C04d_3a and C04e_4a (Appendicies A-C) with PDFs. No other corrections. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Proposals are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 12363N26R4014 is issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) for the Bitterroot Front G-Z Long Term Integrated Resource Service Contract. The Bitterroot Front Project area spans roughly 145,000 acres across the Stevensville and Darby Ranger Districts, where dense, overstocked mixed?conifer stands and widespread tree mortality have increased susceptibility to insect outbreaks and extreme wildfire behavior. Following a decade of severe fires, the project aims to reduce wildfire risk to nearby communities and restore forest health through treatments such as thinning, harvesting, mechanical fuel reduction, and prescribed burning. These efforts focus on improving stand vigor, promoting fire?adapted species, reducing hazardous fuels, and enhancing safety and effectiveness for wildfire responders. A secondary objective of the long?term contract is to provide a consistent timber supply for local forest products industries, while contractors complete tasks including unit layout, timber cruising, road work, and timber removal as part of a broader strategy to increase the pace and scale of forest restoration. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 113310 and the small business size standard is 500 Employees This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency. Proposals are to be submitted via email to Mark Phillipp at mark.phillipp@usda.gov and Matt Daigle at matthew.daigle@usda.gov.

title: Stage 2 - Sidney Operations Centre Marine Fuel & Docks Replacement, Gulf Islands National Park Reserve
description: Parks Canada Agency has a requirement for a Contractor to replace the existing docks and marine fueling system at the Sidney Operations Centre (SOC), located at 2220 Harbour Road in Sidney, British Columbia, which serves as the primary Parks Canada Agency office and marine operations base for the Gulf Islands National Park Reserve. The work includes the removal, disposal, and replacement of the existing docks, pilings, and associated servicing systems. The Contractor will supply and install new aluminum-frame docks, pilings, water and electrical services, dock lighting, and a new fueling system consisting of a 5,000-litre fuel tank, fuel lines, and dispenser. All in-water works, including the removal of the existing docks and pilings and the installation of the new docks, must be completed within the lower-risk fisheries window between December 1, 2026, and February 15, 2027. Work occurring above the high-water line may be completed outside of this period. The Contractor will be required to implement the mitigation measures identified in Parks Canada Agency’s Basic Impact Assessment to minimize environmental risks and impacts associated with the project. TWO STAGE SELECTION PROCESS This posting is the Stage Two of a two-stage solicitation process: the first stage was to evaluate the qualifications of all interested suppliers. The second stage (Stage Two) is to invite the qualified suppliers to provide further qualifications and a financial bid on the project based on the specifications and drawings. Only qualified suppliers have been invited to bid. Potential and interested sub-contractors are invited to add their company’s name under the section “Partner with another business”.

title: Lead Hazardous Waste Removal for RCMP Indoor Firing Ranges (IFR), Alberta
description: This requirement is for the Royal Canadian Mounted Police. This requirement is open only to those Supply Arrangement Holders under EW479-162880 who can perform the services in the geographical location of Alberta. The requirement is intended to result in the award of one (1) contract. The following Supply Arrangement Holders have been invited to submit a proposal: Stericycle Aevitas Clean Harbors Canada Inc. and Affiliated Companies GFL Environmental Inc. KBL Environmental Ltd. Shield Specialize Emergency Services Inc. Veolia es Canada Services Industriels Inc. Miller Environmental SUMAS Environmental Services Quest Disposal & Recycling Environmental 360 Solutions Description of the Requirement: Lead Hazardous Waste Removal for RCMP Indoor Firing Ranges (IFR), Alberta The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) K Division, Real Property and Asset Management has a requirement for the cleaning, removal, packing, disposal and/or recycling of hazardous waste materials from four RCMP Indoor Firing ranges located in Edmonton, Red Deer, Edson and St. Paul, Alberta. Level of Security Requirement: Resource Minimum Security Level Required: RCMP Facility Access Level 2 with Escort (FA2) Applicable Trade Agreements: Canada Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Columbia Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement, Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement, Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement, Canada-Ukraine Free Trade Agreement, Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), and World Trade Organization – Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-AGP) Proposed period of contract: The proposed period of contract shall be for one year from date of contract award inclusive, with the irrevocable option to extend the term of the Contract by up to three additional one year periods under the same conditions. Estimated Level of Effort: The estimated level of effort of the contract, per year and across all 4 locations, will be: 10 times per year : Using steel rod, check the depth of rubber pellets from surface of trap to rigid steps of the bullet trap structure or new lead buildup in the middle of trap and its both corners. Add rubber pellets into bullet trap to maintain 600mm (24 inches) depth. Refill the trap hopper with new rubber pellets. Rake rubber pellets to cover rubber membrane at the back of the trap with rubber pellets. Level rubber berm surface to make proper slope. 5 times per year: Fix, patch, and/or flip rubber curtains if applicable 4 times per year: Replacement of rubber curtains or panels if applicable 4 times per year: Lead mining of the bullet trap system 4 times per year: Deep cleaning of firing range, range walls 1.8m AFF, training gear (e.g., target holders, First Air kit, etc.), all horizontal surfaces, control and gun cleaning rooms, floors, HEPA vacuum inside filter sections of supply and exhaust units 5 times per year: Replacement of pre-filters for exhaust ventilation unit HEPA filters replacement must be coordinated with Project Authority and to be done every 5 years (for Edson, St. Paul, and Red Deer sites), and every 4 years (Edmonton HQ) The estimated level of effort provided is for bid evaluated price determination purposes only. Their inclusion does not represent a commitment by Canada that Canada’s future usage of the services described in the bid solicitation will be consistent with this data. The RFSA will remain valid until such time as Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) no longer considers it to be advantageous to use it.

title: Ireland – Social research services – Request for Tenders for the Provision of a Rapid Evidence Assessment in relation to reading for pleasure among children and young people in Ireland with a particular focus on boys and young men
description: The Department of Education and Youth is seeking research services from a suitably qualified contractor/s to conduct a rapid evidence review in relation to reading for pleasure among children and young people in Ireland, with a particular focus on boys and young men. For the purposes of this review, the terms children and young people and boys and young men refer to learners from the early learning and care (ELC) sector through primary and post-primary education. The review should therefore consider evidence relating to attitudes, engagement and participation in reading for pleasure across the continuum of educational provision, including key developmental and educational transition points.

title: Ireland – Social research services – Request for Tender for the provision of a rapid evidence review in relation to confidence in maths among children and young people in Ireland with a particular focus on girls and young women
description: The Department is seeking research services from a suitably qualified contractor(s) to conduct a rapid evidence review in relation to confidence in mathematics among children and young people in Ireland, with a particular focus on girls and young women. For the purposes of this review, the terms children and young people and girls and young women refer to learners from the early learning and care (ELC) sector through primary and post-primary education. The review should therefore consider evidence relating to confidence in mathematics and numeracy, including learners' self-belief, mathematical self-efficacy, attitudes towards mathematics, and willingness to engage with mathematical learning across the continuum of educational provision, including key developmental and educational transition points.

Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition sensitive information contained within their response as instructed later in this posting. BACKGROUND AND SCOPE The United States (US) Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance & Special Operations Forces (ISR & SOF) Directorate, Special Warfare (SW) Program Office (AFLCMC/WISN) is conducting market research to identify possible sources capable of providing the NGOCS. CAPABILITY GAP Operators currently lack a lightweight, ruggedized, modular body-worn power, data, and edge-compute architecture capable of providing distributed processing capacity beyond the End User Device (EUD) for concurrent high-demand tactical workloads. Fielded systems rely on aging architecture, proprietary cabling, and limited processing capabilities at the edge. Consequently, the EUD is forced to absorb the entirety of application processing, edge-server hosting, message routing, video data links, and peripheral management. During high-tempo combat operations, this overreliance creates latency, power depletion, and reliability bottlenecks that can jeopardize the mission. title: Coburn Gore LPOE Art in Architecture Project
description: Document Added & Updated: 0332CG-AIA- Coburn Gore AIA Questions & Answers V3 Dated 07 October 2026 The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) Art in Architecture Program commissions American artists (citizens and Lawful Permanent Residents or Permanent Workers of the United States) to create publicly scaled and permanently installed artworks for Federal buildings nationwide. GSA announces an opportunity for a Federal art commission in conjunction with the new construction of the Coburn Gore Land Port of Entry (LPOE) in Coburn, Maine. The new facility will strengthen supply chains, improve operational capabilities and facility infrastructure, spur economic growth, and bolster the country�s security. The project will provide a fully operational LPOE that coordinates with the tra?c ?ow and operations of the Canadian port of entry at Saint-Augustin-de-Woburn Quebec, Port of Entry. The project will provide a new port that allows Customs and Border Protection to more efficiently carry out its agency mission, their operations and interactions with the public. GSA allocates one-half of one percent (0.5%) of the estimated construction costs of new or modernized Federal facilities for art commissions. The art budget for this project is estimated to be between $275,000 to $400,000. One or more artists will be awarded a fixed-price contract for a commission. Artists who wish to be considered for this GSA art commission must submit application materials to GSA by the SAM Contract Opportunity�s Response Date. Artists may also elect to be considered for all future GSA art commissions by submitting application materials to GSA�s National Artist Registry (Registry). title: El Toro Range Improvements
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This notice is issued solely for market research and planning purposes to determine the availability and capability of qualified sources under NAICS 236220. The Government is seeking responses from both small and large business concerns. This is not a solicitation, and no contract will be awarded from this notice. Project Overview: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is conducting market research for a potential Design-Build requirement supporting improvements to a range in the Irvine, California area. The anticipated scope includes restroom upgrades, erosion control, concrete pad installation, electrical upgrades, and large-scale asphalt pavement repair. The estimated magnitude is between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. A brief outline of the work is below: Electrical System Upgrade Provide and install a 225?kVA transformer (208Y/120V, 3?phase) and a 600?amp main distribution panel. Erosion Control (25? and 50?Yard Ranges) Conduct geotechnical borings and design a compliant erosion control system (retaining structures, drainage). Construct stabilization measures, install drainage, and provide as?built documentation. Pavement Rehabilitation (~30,000 SY) Assess roadway conditions and drainage patterns. Perform milling, full?depth asphalt repairs, subgrade stabilization, HMA paving, compaction, and final striping. Restroom Renovations Fully renovate two commercial restrooms, including demolition, framing, waterproofing, electrical, plumbing, fixtures, finishes, and accessibility components. Water Pressure Improvements Assess existing domestic water system and design a solution to increase operating pressure to 60�70 psi. Furnish and install all new equipment, controls, piping, and backflow prevention. Range Concrete Improvements (25?Yard Pad & Lane Markings) Survey, grade, and install new concrete pad, walking paths, and reinforced firing lanes. Install or tie into an existing lead?collection system. Provide durable, visible lane markings at the 3, 5, 7, 15, and 25?yard distances Required Capabilities: Respondents should demonstrate experience in design-build construction projects of similar magnitude and complexity, including: restroom renovations, water pressure system installation, slope stabilization/erosion control, concrete pad construction, range marking, electrical upgradess, and asphalt roadway rehabilitation. Submission Requirements: Interested firms should submit a capabilities statement (no more than 10 pages) including but not limited to the following information: � Company name, address, UEI, CAGE code, business size and socioeconomic status. � Bonding capability (single and aggregate). � Relevant project experience within the past 5 years. � Ability to perform work in Southern California. � Availability of personnel capable of meeting FBI security requirements (US Citizens only) � Statement of interest in performing as a prime contractor. Submission Instructions: Responses shall be submitted via email to the following: Amanda Mobley, Contracting Officer � almobley@fbi.gov Disclaimer: This Sources Sought Notice is for informational purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. No reimbursement will be provided for any costs incurred in preparing a response. The Government has not determined the acquisition strategy and will evaluate capabilities from both small and large business concerns.

title: FORT PIERCE HARBOR MAINTENANCE DREDGING, ST. LUCIE COUNTY, FLORIDA
description: PROJECT DESCRIPTION: Project work includes maintenance dredging of Fort Pierce Harbor with excavated material being placed onto Fort Pierce Beach. Due to the extensive hardbottom areas located offshore of the fill area, offshore pipeline access to the beach site is prohibited. Offloading the beach fill will be done inside the South Jetty of Fort Pierce Inlet, as shown on the drawings. A staging area and beach access to the beach placement area are located at the end of Seaway Drive and near the south jetty pumpout location. Work also includes but is not limited to environmental and water quality monitoring, sea turtle trawl sweeping (hopper dredges only), screening, beach tilling, beach fill quality control, construction support, and vibration control and monitoring. Work will be divided into a base and two options. BIDS DUE: 22 October 2026 at 1:00 PM EDT. NAICS CODE: 237990, OTHER HEAVY CIVIL ENGINEERING CONSTRUCTION. SMALL BUSINESS SIZE STANDARD: $37 million. TARGET PRICE RANGE: Between $5,000,000.00 and $10,000,000.00. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: The Contractor shall be required to (a) commence work under this contract within SIXTY (60) calendar days after the date the Contractor receives the Notice to Proceed (NTP), (b) prosecute the work diligently, and (c) complete the entire work ready for use, and be off the beach, not later than 30 May 2027, with 30 June 2027 for the entire contract work. The time stated for completion shall include final cleanup of the premises. The completion date is based on the assumption that the successful offeror will receive the notice to proceed by 7 January 2027. The completion date will be extended by the number of calendar days after the above date that the Contractor receives the notice to proceed, except to the extent that the delay in issuance of the notice to proceed results from the failure of the Contractor to execute the contract and give the required performance and payment bonds within the time specified in the offer.

It is for informational and planning purposes and shall NOT be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation or commitment by the Government at this time. PTOEA The Government contemplates utilizing the Alternative Competition Method in accordance with the Patent and Trademark Office Acquisition Guidelines (PTAG) and the Patent and Trademark Office Efficiency Act 35 U.S.C. � 2(b)(4)(A). This Sources sought notice is intended as preliminary market information gathering by which the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) will determine which contractor(s) is/are the most likely to successfully meet the agency�s needs and are thereby eligible to participate in an alternative competition. As a result of this market research, if a solicitation is issued, it will only be issued to the/ those qualified contractor(s) that is/are deemed most likely to successfully meet the agency�s requirements as stated below. This RFI is being made available under NAICS 561312 � Executive Search Services and PSC R431 Support�Professional: Human Resources The purpose of this Sources Sought / Request for Information (RFI) Notice 1. Background The USPTO is a federal agency in the Department of Commerce (DOC), which is headquartered in Alexandria, VA. The mission of the USPTO is to foster innovation and competitiveness by providing high quality and timely examination and issuance of patent and trademark applications, guiding domestic and international intellectual property policy, and delivering intellectual property information and education worldwide. Through the issuance of patents, the USPTO encourages technological advancement by providing incentives to invent, invest in, and disclose new technology worldwide. Through the registration of trademarks, the agency assists businesses in protecting their investments, promoting goods and services, and safeguarding consumers against confusion and deception in the marketplace. The office employs over 13,000 full-time staff to support its work. 2. Objectives The USPTO is seeking to establish a single-award Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) with a firm specializing in executive-level recruitment. The ideal partner will possess a proven track record of sourcing high-caliber passive candidates through proprietary networks, global executive databases, and direct headhunting methodologies. The vendor must demonstrate the ability to identify and attract diverse, competitive talent for Senior Executive Service (SES) and Senior Level (SL) equivalent roles, with a specific focus on passive candidates currently employed in top-tier organizations across the following disciplines: Patent, Trademark, Information Technology, Finance, Cyber Security, General Law, and Administrative Services. 3. Abbreviated Scope of Work This effort is for executive search services to identify, deliver and recruit highly qualified candidates for identified USPTO SES and/or SL vacancies and to have those candidates submit applications through USAJobs for the specified vacancies. The contractor shall ensure that all identified candidates possess the required professional, technical and executive core qualifications as outlined in the attached position description associated with each vacancy and as outlined by each specific call order. The contractor shall present a detailed recruitment plan for each specified vacancy, that provides a detailed approach to marketing, searching for candidates, and the process for assisting the candidate with the USAJobs application process.The contractor shall maintain a record of contact/information exchange with all contractors identified candidates and notify the USPTO when their identified candidate(s) have submitted their application to USAJobs. The contractor shall provide weekly status reports to the USPTO outlining progress related to the specified search. 4. Deliverables Deliverables shall carry over to each BPA Call as follows: EVENT 1: Draft Recruitment Plan DELIVERY DATE: Date of Proposal Submission EVENT 2: Kick-Off Meeting DELIVERY DATE: Within five (5) business from award (to be scheduled by the Government) EVENT 3: Final Recruitment Plan DELIVERY DATE: Five (5) days after Kick-off Meeting EVENT 4: Application Notification DELIVERY DATE: Within 2 business days of applicant submitting via USAJobs, as applicable 4. Special Requirements For the applicants to be considered for the position, their application package must be successfully uploaded to the USAJobs.gov website, unless otherwise specified by the specific call order. Applications must meet the requirements that will be stated in the vacancy announcement by the closing date of the posting. 5. Place of Performance a) This work will be performed via virtual recruitment and/or at the contractor�s offsite location. b) All work related to this contract shall be performed in the United States (U.S.) and legally authorized U.S. territories (American Samoa, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands), at either the USPTO�s campus in Alexandria, Virginia, the Contractors� and subcontractors� facilities authorized in the USPTO granted Authorization to Operate (ATO), and/or from USPTO approved telework locations. Work at any other location is prohibited unless authorized by the Contracting Officer. This shall be construed to include all means of telecommunication access to the ATO system and supporting infrastructure as well. c) Any work authorized pursuant to this contract under a telework provision, for any reason, is subject to the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR) approval. The following additional requirements must also be met: All authorized telework shall be conducted solely on USPTO authorized systems, devices, and baseline configurations over USPTO approved remote access systems and access technologies. All authorized telework shall only access USPTO and/or Contractor networks and systems within the system boundary from the approved telework location set forth in the Telework Agreement. All authorized telework shall only access USPTO and/or Contractor networks and system via connection authorized by the USPTO granted ATO. No data shall be transferred for ANY reasons to systems and/or devices outside of the authorized secure system boundary of the USPTO granted ATO. The Contractor shall be responsible for any costs/expenses associated in making its staff telework ready. At no time shall any USPTO provided equipment be permitted outside of the U.S. and legally authorized U.S. territories. 6. Estimated Period of Performance The USPTO anticipates awarding a BPA with a Base year + 4 Option Years. 7. Estimated Volume The USPTO anticipates multiple executive searches annually, but an estimated number of searches is not available at this time. The responses to this RFI should provide USPTO management with an understanding of the experience and the range of executive services provided. This will allow USPTO management to conduct thorough market research, identify suitable providers, and make informed decisions. See SF1449 and Related Attachments for details The solicitation will be a fixed-priced time charter with reimbursable elements, with a performance period of one (1) year base period and will be followed by three (3) 1-year option periods and one 11-month option period. The solicitation will require a time charter of one US flagged or foreign flagged vessel (to be reflagged US prior to delivery of vessel) required to tow an acoustic array in support of U.S. Navy Operations. The vessel will tow a passive acoustic monitoring system, between 4-6 knots, 24hrs/day for up to a 60-day event. The ship will need to be able to tow on a directed heading within 5 degrees for extended periods at slow speed. Because of the type of acoustic system employed, the ability of the vessel to maintain heading stability is critical. The vessel must be capable of worldwide operations, including support in all ocean basins of the world from the Artic to the Antarctic during all periods of time. The vessel is expected to operate in open water in the vicinity of the Marginal Ice Zone (MIZ) and must be capable of surviving encounter with young open ice, as specified by ABS, Ice Class D0.

title: Design-Build Maintenance and Repair Army Reserve (MRAR) of Equipment Concentration Site (ECS), B-56767, at North Cavazos, TX
description: Request for Proposal (RFP), Solicitation No. W912QR25RA013 is issued for the repair of a failing Equipment Concentration Site (ECS), B-56767, at North Cavazos, TX. This project will repair and construct an addition to an existing ~26,000 square feet of the maintenance part of the Equipment Concentration Site, Maintenance Building 56767, that is in a failing condition, and has not undergone any major infrastructure or system repairs, only limited maintenance and repair work has occurred. The project includes repair of HVAC and Electrical systems, remove non-structural interior walls to right-size rooms and create open flexible workspace, restore inadequate and non-code compliant bathrooms, repair light fixtures with code compliant units, failed flooring, code compliant fire alarm and suppression system, repair electrical conduit distribution throughout the facility. Access for individuals with disabilities will be provided to include a code compliant entrance ramp. The restored facility will meet minimum DOD Antiterrorism standards. This project contains options. The contract duration is estimated at 913 calendar days from Contract Notice to Proceed (NTP). This award is Subject to the Availability of Funds (SAF). TYPE OF CONTRACT AND NAICS: This RFP will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this effort is 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. TYPE OF SET-ASIDE: Total Small Business Set-Aside Procurement SELECTION PROCESS: This is a two-phase Design/Build procurement. The proposals will be evaluated using a Best-Value Tradeoff (BVTO) source selection process. The technical information contained in each Offeror's proposal will be reviewed, evaluated, and rated by the Government. Potential offerors are invited to submit their past performance, technical, and capability information as described in Section 00 22 16 and Section 00 22 18 of the Solicitation, for review and consideration by the Government. As described in Section 00 22 16 of the Solicitation, the selection process for Phase I will evaluate such factors as Past Performance (for both the Prime Contractor and A/E Designer of Record) and Technical Approach for Design/Build. Pro Forma Information such as bonding and financial capability will also be required to meet the minimum requirements of the solicitation. Following completion of the evaluation of Phase I, a target of five (5) of the most highly qualified offerors will be invited to participate in Phase II. The selected offerors for Phase II will be requested to submit additional information as will be described in Section 00 22 18 of the Solicitation, for review and evaluation by the Government. The selection process for Phase II will evaluate such factors as: Design Narrative, Management Plan, Schedule Narrative, and Price. The Standard Form (SF) 1442 will also be required. (NOTE: The evaluation factors for Phase II provided in Section 00 22 18 are issued as a DRAFT during Phase I and is subject to change with the Phase II amendment.) All evaluation factors, other than cost or price, are considered approximately equal to cost or price. DISCUSSIONS: The Government intends to award without discussions, but reserves the right to conduct discussion should it be deemed in the Government's best interest. CONSTRUCTION MAGNITUDE: The magnitude of this construction project is anticipated to be between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000, in accordance with DFARS 236.204. SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS: Paper copies of the solicitation and amendments will not be issued. Telephone, email, and fax requests for this solicitation, amendments, and attachments (plans and specifications) will not be honored. Project files are Portable Document Format (PDF) files and can be viewed, navigated, or printed using Adobe Acrobat Reader. To be able to download the solicitation for this project, contractors are required to register at the System for Award Management at https://sam.gov. Amendments, when issued, will be posted to the SAM.gov website for electronic downloading. This will be the only method of distributing amendments prior to closing; therefore, it is the Offerors� responsibility to check the websites periodically for any and all amendments to the solicitation. REGISTRATIONS: Offerors shall have and shall maintain an active registration in the following database: System for Award Management (SAM): Offerors shall have and shall maintain an active registration in the SAM database at http://www.sam.gov to be eligible for a Government contract award. If the Offeror is a Joint Venture (JV), the JV entity shall have valid SAM registration in the SAM database representing the JV as one business/firm/entity. If at the time of award an Offeror is not actively and successfully registered in the SAM database, the Government reserves the right to award to the next prospective Offeror. description: *****AMENDMENT 0001 IS ISSUED TO PHASE II SELECTED OFFERORS ONLY ON TUESDAY, 22 SEPTEMBER 2026***** Request for Proposal (RFP), Solicitation No. W912QR25RA013 is issued for the repair of a failing Equipment Concentration Site (ECS), B-56767, at North Fort Hood (formerly Fort Cavazos), TX. This project will repair and construct an addition to an existing ~26,000 square feet of the maintenance part of the Equipment Concentration Site, Maintenance Building 56767, that is in a failing condition, and has not undergone any major infrastructure or system repairs, only limited maintenance and repair work has occurred. The project includes repair of HVAC and Electrical systems, remove non-structural interior walls to right-size rooms and create open flexible workspace, restore inadequate and non-code compliant bathrooms, repair light fixtures with code compliant units, failed flooring, code compliant fire alarm and suppression system, repair electrical conduit distribution throughout the facility. Access for individuals with disabilities will be provided to include a code compliant entrance ramp. The restored facility will meet minimum DOD Antiterrorism standards. This project contains options. The contract duration is estimated at 913 calendar days from Contract Notice to Proceed (NTP). This award is Subject to the Availability of Funds (SAF). NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek resolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the USDA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

title: Custom Integrated Robotic System
description: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source Contract: The Defense Threat Reduction Agency (DTRA), DTRA West Contracting (J4-CRW), Kirtland AFB, NM, intends to award a firm-fixed-price, sole-source contract to Rocky Mountain Unmanned Systems (RMUS) LLC, 1256 W 50 S, Centerville, UT 84014, for the procurement of a Custom-Integrated Robotic System. Requirement Description: The requirement is for an applied research and development R and D effort to design, engineer, integrate, and deliver one (1) functional prototype robotic system. The system must be capable of autonomously navigating hazardous environments and creating a real-time, three-dimensional (3D) Hazardous Atmosphere Map. The core of the requirement is a complex software and systems integration task. The contractor must successfully fuse data from a Government-Furnished multi-gas chemical detector with data streams from a contractor-provided commercial quadrupedal robotic platform, a survey-grade 3D LiDAR sensor, and a tactical mesh networking radio into a single, unified operational picture for the user. Statutory Authority: This acquisition is being conducted under the authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1)as implemented by FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. Rationale for Sole Source: Market research has concluded that RMUS is the only responsible source capable of providing this system without unacceptable risk and schedule delays to the Government. While the hardware components are commercial-off-the-shelf, the unique requirement is the software data-fusion architecture needed to integrate them. RMUS is the sole identified vendor that possesses the pre-existing, proprietary software framework and demonstrated experience required to fuse the specific data streams from these disparate systems into the required 3D hazardous atmosphere map. No other source has demonstrated this unique, pre-existing software capability. The Government does not own a technical data package suitable for competition. Submission of Capability Statements: This notice is not a request for competitive proposals. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. Interested parties must provide clear and convincing evidence that they possess the demonstrated, pre-existing software data-fusion capability to meet the specific requirements described herein. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Please submit any capability statements by email to the points of contact listed below no later than the response date of this notice.

title: Winter Harbor Maintenance Dredging
description: DESCRIPTION THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS OR INVITATION FOR BIDS. NO SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS ARE AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. The Norfolk District, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, is anticipating a future procurement for a firm-fixed-price construction contract for Maintenance Dredging of the Quinby Creek Federal Navigation Channel located in Accomack County, Virginia. DESCRIPTION OF WORK The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Norfolk District, is seeking qualified and experienced firms capable of performing maintenance dredging of the Quinby Creek Federal Navigation Channel in Accomack County, Virginia. The work consists of dredging approximately 200,000 cubic yards of maintenance material from the Federal channel. Dredging will be performed using a hydraulic cutterhead pipeline dredge, with dredged material hydraulically placed within the Government-designated overboard placement site in Upshur Bay. The maximum contract pay depth will be -7 feet mean lower low water (MLLW). In accordance with FAR 36.204(g), the estimated construction price range for this project is between $5,000,000 and $10,000,000. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990, Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The small business size standard applicable to Dredging and Surface Cleanup Activities is $37,000,000. The Government is not obligated to and will not pay for any information received from potential sources as a result of this Sources Sought Notice. CONSTRUCTION TIME The Contractor will be required to commence work within 15 calendar days after receipt of the Notice to Proceed (NTP). The anticipated construction period of performance is approximately 180 calendar days from issuance of the NTP. SURVEY OF THE DREDGING INDUSTRY The following confidential survey questionnaire is designed to apprise the Corps of prospective dredging contractors' project execution capabilities. Please provide responses to the following questions. All questions pertain to the Quinby Creek Maintenance Dredging project in Accomack County, Virginia. Please provide the company's name, address, point of contact, telephone number, and email address. Would your firm be interested in bidding on this requirement if a solicitation is issued? If no, please briefly explain why. Has your firm performed dredging projects similar in nature, complexity, and magnitude to this project within the past five years? Has your firm managed dredged material placement sites with inflows similar in magnitude to this project within the past five years? If so, describe the project(s), identify for whom the work was performed, provide the dollar value of the project(s), and identify a point of contact and telephone number as a reference for the relevant experience. Would your firm bid on this project as a sole contractor, prime contractor with subcontractor(s), or as a joint venture? Is there a dollar limit on the size of contract your firm would bid? If so, what is that limit? What is the largest dredging contract, in dollars, on which your firm was the prime contractor? What is your firm's bonding capacity per contract? What is your firm's total aggregate bonding capacity? Identify your firm's business size and all applicable socioeconomic categories, including Large Business, Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business, and Women-Owned Small Business. Is your firm familiar with the safety and health requirements of EM 385-1-1? Please include only a concise narrative addressing the requested information. Additional information may not be reviewed. This Sources Sought Notice should not be construed as an obligation by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Norfolk District, to issue a solicitation or award a contract, nor does it create any right to reimbursement for costs incurred in responding to this notice. No solicitation is currently available. The Government will use the information received to assist in determining the appropriate acquisition strategy. All prospective contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at SAM.gov prior to contract award. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice must be submitted no later than 22 October 2026 via email to LTC George Jackson at george.jackson@usace.army.mil and Luke D. Hedlund at luke.d.hedlund@usace.army.mil. Any future solicitation for this requirement will be issued through SAM.gov.

title: Craney Island Rehandling Basin Dredging
description: DESCRIPTION OF WORK The work consists of maintenance dredging, hydraulic placement of dredged material, and debris removal at the Craney Island Rehandling Basin. The project is located on the southeast side of the Craney Island Dredged Material Management Area (CIDMMA), adjacent to the Norfolk Harbor Channel in Portsmouth, Virginia. Maintenance dredging and debris removal will occur in the following areas: � North Access Channel to a depth of -18 feet MLLW � South Access Channel to a depth of -18 feet MLLW � Debris Channel to a depth of -9 feet MLLW � Rehandling Basin to a depth of -20 feet MLLW Optional bid items will include increased dredging depth within the Rehandling Basin to -23 feet MLLW. The estimated quantity for the base work is approximately 260,000 cubic yards of dredged material, including allowable overdepth and anticipated accretion. Debris, including wire, rope, steel, and wood, may be encountered during dredging operations and shall be managed and removed by the Contractor. All dredged material shall be hydraulically transported by pipeline and placed at the Government-furnished upland placement site within the Craney Island Dredged Material Management Area. CONSTRUCTION DURATION The Contractor shall commence performance within 15 calendar days after receipt of the Notice to Proceed (NTP) and complete all work within 180 calendar days. There are no known dredging time-of-year restrictions associated with this project. Identify the type of dredge plant and supporting equipment your firm owns and/or operates that would be suitable for this requirement. Describe your firm's experience managing upland dredged material placement sites with inflow volumes similar to this project. Indicate whether your firm would compete as a prime contractor, as part of a joint venture, or with subcontractors. Provide your firm's bonding capacity, both single-project and aggregate. Identify your firm's business size and all applicable socioeconomic categories, including Large Business, Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), and Women-Owned Small Business (WOSB). description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This is not a solicitation or a request for proposal and no contract will be awarded from this notice. No solicitation or specifications are available at this time. Please monitor sam.gov as this Sources Sought Notice will not be linked to the solicitation. The General Services Administration (GSA), Acquisition Project Delivery Division, is conducting market research to determine if any SDVOSB, HUB Zone, EDWOSB or 8(a) Small Business Concern has the current relevant qualifications, experience, personnel, and capability to perform the work described herein. All interested Small Business firms should respond. This Sources Sought Notice is being issued by the General Services Administration (GSA), Acquisition Project Delivery for tenant fit-out Construction services for the United States Coast Guard (USCG) Northeast District to support mission-critical operations across the Northeast maritime region. The place of performance will be the John F. Kennedy (JFK) Federal Building (FB), located at 15 New Sudbury St, Boston, MA 02203. This is a Repair and Alteration (R&A) project which includes operational, administrative, secure, forensic, and mission-support spaces, with construction of a specialized Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) being a particularly important element. Work also includes integrated mission-specific systems such as reliable power, 24/7 HVAC, communications/IT infrastructure, security systems, laboratory support, resilient infrastructure, and an emergency generator. Contractors should anticipate a complex, schedule-sensitive federal fit-out requiring secure construction practices, specialized space coordination, and close integration of architectural, mechanical, electrical, communications, security, and technology systems. Estimated Construction Cost Range is $15,000,000 and $25,000,000.00. Period of Performance is approximately 36 months from date of Notice to Proceed. NAICS Code: Construction of Buildings - 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction with a size standard of $45 Million. PSC Code: Z2AA -- Repair or Alteration of Office Buildings All qualified Small Businesses are encouraged to respond. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. The main purposes of this Sources Sought Notice is to assist the Contracting Officer in determining if a Set-Aside is the acceptable strategy for the procurement. It is requested that interested parties submit a brief capabilities package. The package shall address, at a minimum, the following: Examples of projects worked within the last five years of similar size, scope, complexity and duration as the work indicated. State whether your firm worked as a prime or subcontractor, contract value, brief description of how the referenced contract relates to the work described and provide an agency or owner point of contact. Company profile, to include number of employees, annual receipts, office location(s), and SAM UEI. Evidence to establish your company's standing as a SDVOSB, HUBZone, EDWOSB or 8(a) small business concern, under applicable NAICS. Describe how you will provide a fair market price given the geographical location of this project. A positive statement of your intention to submit a bid for this requirement if set-aside for your socio-economic group. AGAIN, THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. Responses must contain sufficient detail for the Government to make an informed decision regarding your capabilities. Responses must be received no later than 2:00 PM, Local Time on October 22, 2026. Please submit your capability statement via e-mail to Molly A. Lewis, Contract Officer, at Molly.Lewis@gsa.gov. Questions regarding this notice may be addressed to Molly.Lewis@gsa.gov. Failure to submit all information requested will result in a contractor not being considered as an interested small business concern.

title: Maintenance Dredging of the Winter Harbor Federal Navigation Channel
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. THERE WILL NOT BE A SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME. The Norfolk District, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, is anticipating a future procurement for a Firm, Fixed Price Construction Contract for Maintenance Dredging of the Winter Harbor Federal Navigation Channel located in Mathews County, Virginia. Description of Work: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Norfolk District is seeking qualified and experienced firms capable of performing maintenance dredging of shoaled areas from the Winter Harbor Federal Navigation Channel located in Mathews County, Virginia by hydraulic pipeline method with placement of the dredged material in the Government-furnished shoreline placement area located north of the channel. The base work will include dredging approximately 101,000 cubic yards (CY) of sandy material between Stations 30+00 and 78+00 to a required depth of -6.0 feet mean lower low water (MLLW) with one (1) foot of allowable overdepth, for a total project depth of -7.0 feet MLLW in the pay prism. Optional work will include dredging approximately 29,000 CY of additional sandy material between Stations 30+00 and 78+00 an additional one (1) foot of depth, for a total project depth of -8.0 feet MLLW in the pay prism. The hydraulic pipeline pumping distance from the dredging area to the shoreline placement area will be approximately 9,500 linear feet. Dredging will be required for the full channel width from Stations 30+00 to 40+00 and 50+00 to 78+00, and the full channel width plus a 25-foot overcut from Station 40+00 to 50+00 on the north side of the channel and from Station 42+00 to 50+00 on the south side of the channel to remove a significant shoaled area which is blocking the entrance to Winter Harbor. The project will require the dredging of approximately 101,000 CY of material with an option to dredge an additional 29,000 CY, including estimated accretion to October 2027 and allowable overdepth. The contract is anticipated to be a combination of base work and optional work. The base bid will include mobilization and demobilization of all necessary equipment to perform the work and hydraulic pipeline dredging with direct placement in the unconfined Government-furnished shoreline placement area located north of the channel. The estimated construction price range for this project is between $1,000,000 and $5,000,000. NAICS Code 237990 � Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction applies. The Government is not obligated to and will not pay for any information received from potential sources as a result of this synopsis. Construction Time: The construction period of performance will be 120 calendar days from issuance of the NTP. Dredging is prohibited from April 1 to October 31 of any given year due to an environmental time of year restriction. Definitive Responsibility Criteria: This requirement will use Definitive Responsibility Criteria (DRC), which are specific and objective standards established to inform the Contracting Officer, in accordance with FAR 9.104-2. These criteria will be used to assess whether the apparent low bidder can demonstrate the expertise and specialized facilities needed for adequate contract performance. The inability of a contractor otherwise eligible for award to demonstrate minimally acceptable experience as measured by the DRC may result in the Contracting Officer determining the contractor is not responsible. The Definitive Responsibility Criteria will be developed to assess the following work items: Experience in performing a minimum of one hydraulic pipeline dredging job in bay and coastal environments pumping a minimum of 50,000 cubic yards (cy) a distance of two miles or greater within the past five years. Experience in performing a minimum of one job with placement of dredged material within an unconfined nearshore environment (such as beach, surf zone and/or adjacent shallow water areas) similar to the requirements and magnitude of this project within the past five years. Sources are sought for all interested firms with a NAICS code of 237990 with a small business size standard of $37,000,000. SURVEY OF THE DREDGING INDUSTRY The following confidential survey questionnaire is designed to apprise the Corps of prospective dredging contractors' project execution capabilities. Please provide your response to the following questions. All questions are in regard to the Maintenance Dredging of the Winter Harbor Federal Navigation Channel Project located in Mathews County, Virginia. Please provide company�s name, address, point of contact, phone number, and e-mail address. Would you be interested in bidding on the solicitation when it is issued? If the answer is No, please explain why not? Have you worked on dredging jobs similar in nature, complexity and magnitude to this project within the past 5 years? Have you managed the dredge material placement sites with the inflows similar in magnitude to this project in the past 5 years? If so, please describe the project(s) and for whom the work was performed. Indicate the dollar value of the project(s). Identify a point of contact (s) and phone number, as a reference of relevant experience. Would you be bidding on this project as a sole contractor, prime contractor with subcontractor(s) or as a joint venture? Is there a dollar limit on the size of contract that you would bid? If so, what is that limit? What is the largest dredging contract, in dollars, on which you were the prime contractor? What is your bonding capacity per contract? What is your total bonding capacity? Firm's Business Size - LB, SB, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, or WOB. Are you familiar with the safety and health requirements of EM 385-1-1? Please only include a narrative of the requested information. Additional information will not be reviewed. This Sources Sought should not be construed in any manner to be an obligation of the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Norfolk District to issues a contract, or result in any claim for reimbursement of costs for any effort you expand responding to this request. No solicitation is currently available. The Government will utilize this information in determining an acquisition strategy. Please state all of the socio-economic categories in which your company belongs (8)(a), Hub-zone, Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Woman Owned). Please submit capability packages electronically to email to LTC George Jackson at george.jackson@usace.army.mil and Luke Hedlund at luke.d.hedlund@usace.army.mil. The responses to this Sources Sought must be submitted no later than 22 October 2026 via email to LTC George Jackson at george.jackson@usace.army.mil and Luke Hedlund at luke.d.hedlund@usace.army.mil. The official synopsis citing the solicitation number will be issued on SAM.gov at https://sam.gov/content/home . All prospective contractors are required to be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database prior to contract award. Offerors and contractors may obtain information on registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220 or via the Internet at https://www.sam.gov . Representations and Certifications Applications apply to this solicitation. Representations and Certifications may be completed online via the SAM. No attachments or links have been added to this opportunity.

title: Physical Access Control System (PACS) Refresh & Maintenance
description: This Notice of Intent to Sole Source to Siemens for the refresh and maintenance of a Physical Access Control System (PACS) for building security at United States Army Corps of Engineers Detroit District Headquarters located in Detroit, Michigan and will sole source to: Siemens Industry Inc. 1000 E. Deerfield PKWY Buffalo Grove, IL 60089 As part of this procurement, the Detroit Distract intends to specify brand name products on a sole source basis under the authority of Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation Overhaul (RFO) 6.103-1(b) to Siemens Industry Inc. Due to the highly specialized nature of this Software Support Agreement, Siemens is uniquely qualified since it allows the Detroit District Headquarters to maintain a 24/7 emergency contact to keep the C-CURE system fully functional. Work under this contract is expected to include the following: The objective of this project is to procure the necessary hardware, software, and services to upgrade and maintain the existing PACS. The Contractor shall provide all necessary equipment, labor, and expertise to meet the requirements. The Contractor shall provide a renewal for the C?CURE 9000 Software Support Agreement. The agreement is necessary to receive technical support, software updates, and patches. The contractor shall have Direct Support attached to the support agreement at time of renewal. The Contractor shall purchase, program, and install thirteen (13) new card readers to replace the current proximity-only readers. The Contractor shall upgrade the C?CURE 9000 software from the current version (2.9) to the latest stable and approved version (e.g., Version 3.1 or higher) for continued secure operation. The Contractor will provide an Emergency Onsite Response service between scheduled service calls and respond onsite at your facility within the next business day, Monday through Friday, excluding federal holidays, during the hours of 8:00 AM � 5:00 PM (Eastern Standard Time) for emergency conditions, as determined by Detroit District. This notice of intent is not a request for a competitive proposal. This is not a solicitation and the information contained herein are subject to change or be eliminated from the requirement. Only Contractor's capable of providing directly compatible equivalent products shall respond. Oral communications are not acceptable in response to this notice. Interested parties who feel they have the capability may identify their interest and capabilities to provide directly compatible equivalent products, please provide the following: 1. Name of Firm 2. Cage Code 3. Point of Contact, Phone Number, and Email address 4. Supporting documentation to illustrate the directly compatible equivalent products/services/software Submit and information for consideration by the Government to sally.e.artz@usace.army.mil, matthew.mcduffie@usace.army.mil, and LRE-Proposal@usace.army.mil, Subject: Notice of Intent to Sole Source to Siemens. Responses shall be evaluated solely for the purpose of determining whether or not to conduct this procurement on a competitive basis. A determination by the government to not compete this proposed contract, based upon responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government.

title: Design-Build Maintenance and Repair Army Reserve (MRAR) of Equipment Concentration Site (ECS), B-56767, at North Fort Hood, TX
description: *****THE PHASE II SITE VISIT SIGN-IN SHEET IS POSTED ON WEDNESDAY, 07 OCTOBER 2026***** *****AMENDMENT 0001 WAS ISSUED TO PHASE II SELECTED OFFERORS ONLY ON TUESDAY, 22 SEPTEMBER 2026***** Request for Proposal (RFP), Solicitation No. W912QR25RA013 is issued for the repair of a failing Equipment Concentration Site (ECS), B-56767, at North Fort Hood (formerly Fort Cavazos), TX. This project will repair and construct an addition to an existing ~26,000 square feet of the maintenance part of the Equipment Concentration Site, Maintenance Building 56767, that is in a failing condition, and has not undergone any major infrastructure or system repairs, only limited maintenance and repair work has occurred. The project includes repair of HVAC and Electrical systems, remove non-structural interior walls to right-size rooms and create open flexible workspace, restore inadequate and non-code compliant bathrooms, repair light fixtures with code compliant units, failed flooring, code compliant fire alarm and suppression system, repair electrical conduit distribution throughout the facility. Access for individuals with disabilities will be provided to include a code compliant entrance ramp. The restored facility will meet minimum DOD Antiterrorism standards. This project contains options. The contract duration is estimated at 913 calendar days from Contract Notice to Proceed (NTP). This award is Subject to the Availability of Funds (SAF). TYPE OF CONTRACT AND NAICS: This RFP will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract. The North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this effort is 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction. TYPE OF SET-ASIDE: Total Small Business Set-Aside Procurement SELECTION PROCESS: This is a two-phase Design/Build procurement. The proposals will be evaluated using a Best-Value Tradeoff (BVTO) source selection process. The technical information contained in each Offeror's proposal will be reviewed, evaluated, and rated by the Government. Phase II Selected Offerors are requested to submit additional information described in Section 00 22 18 of the Solicitation, for review and evaluation by the Government. The selection process for Phase II will evaluate such factors as: Design Narrative, Management Plan, Schedule Narrative, and Price. The Standard Form (SF) 1442, resubmission of Evidence of Ability to Obtain Bonding and Proof of Financial Ability, and resubmission of Pre-Award Information will also be required. All evaluation factors, other than cost or price, are considered approximately equal to cost or price. NEGOTIATIONS: The Government intends to award without negotiations, but reserves the right to conduct negotiations should it be deemed in the Government's best interest. ESTIMATED CONSTRUCTION COST: The estimated construction cost is anticipated to be between $10,000,000 and $25,000,000. SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS: Paper copies of the solicitation and amendments will not be issued. Telephone, email, and fax requests for this solicitation, amendments, and attachments (plans and specifications) will not be honored. Project files are Portable Document Format (PDF) files and can be viewed, navigated, or printed using Adobe Acrobat Reader. To be able to download the solicitation for this project, contractors are required to register at the System for Award Management at https://sam.gov and have a profile at the Procurement Integrated Envrionment Enterprise (PIEE) website at https://cac.piee.eb.mil/xhtml/auth/home/home.xhtml#. description: SOURCES SOUGHT / REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) Power Distribution and Illumination Systems, Electrical (PDISE) The PM E2S2 has a potential requirement for the build-to-print manufacture, assembly, first article inspection, preproduction First Article testing, and delivery of the PDISE family of systems and associated components and packaging. PDISE is a standardized, ruggedized, man-portable family of electrical feeder and distribution equipment that connect mobile power generation equipment and warfighter mission equipment in harsh tactical environments across Multi-Domain Operations (MDO). The PDISE family consists of five Government-owned Technical Data Package (TDP) end-item Configuration Items (CIs) and their associated accessories. For this acquisition, only four of those end-items are required. The M60 A/P Distribution System is not anticipated to be included in this acquisition effort. The following systems will be procured: M200 A/P Feeder System: 3-Phase, 200 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/1; Drawing 13229E6350) (NSN 6150-01-308-5672) M100 A/P Feeder System: 3-Phase, 100 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/2; Drawing 13229E6351) (NSN 6150-01-308-5671) M40 A/P Distribution System: 3-Phase, 40 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/3; Drawing 13229E6353) (NSN 6150-01-307-9446) M46 Utility Assembly: Electrical Receptacles and Illumination Kit (MIL-DTL-53126/5; Drawing 13226E7046) (NSN 6150-01-208-9751) Procurement Baseline: Build-to-print execution using existing Government TDPs, MIL-DTL-53126, and associated specification slash sheets. TDPs for the PDISE systems are available upon request. The Government seeks to determine: The availability of qualified large and small business sources under NAICS 335999 and 335313 capable of manufacturing, testing, and delivering the PDISE family of systems. Industry capacity and lead times for manufacturing and assembling heavy-duty electrical power-distribution equipment, including Class L connectors, ruggedized cables, military packaging and specialized circuit breakers. description: SOURCES SOUGHT / REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) Power Distribution and Illumination Systems, Electrical (PDISE) Issuing Agency: Department of the Army, Army Contracting Command � Aberdeen Proving Ground (ACC-APG), Belvoir Division Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE): PAE Agile Sustainment & Ammunition (PAE ASA) Project Manager (PM): PM Expeditionary Energy and Sustainment Systems (PM E2S2) NAICS Code: 335999 (Miscellaneous Electrical Equipment and Component Manufacturing) and 335313 (Switchgear and Switchboard Apparatus Manufacturing) PSC / FSC Code: 6150 (Miscellaneous Electric Power and Distribution Equipment) Classification Code: 61 (Electric wire, and power and distribution equipment) Notice Type: Sources Sought / Request for Information (Market Research under FAR Part 10) 1.0 DISCLAIMER & SPECIAL NOTICES This is a Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought Synopsis issued solely for information and planning purposes in accordance with FAR 15.201(e) and FAR Part 10. This notice does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not pay for information submitted in response to this RFI, nor will it reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparing responses. Proprietary information, if any, should be minimized and MUST BE CLEARLY MARKED. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. 2.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND & SCOPE The PM E2S2 has a potential requirement for the build-to-print manufacture, assembly, first article inspection, preproduction First Article testing, and delivery of the PDISE family of systems and associated components and packaging. PDISE is a standardized, ruggedized, man-portable family of electrical feeder and distribution equipment that connect mobile power generation equipment and warfighter mission equipment in harsh tactical environments across Multi-Domain Operations (MDO). The PDISE family consists of five Government-owned Technical Data Package (TDP) end-item Configuration Items (CIs) and their associated accessories. For this acquisition, only four of those end-items are required. The M60 A/P Distribution System is not anticipated to be included in this acquisition effort. The following systems will be procured: M200 A/P Feeder System: 3-Phase, 200 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/1; Drawing 13229E6350) (NSN 6150-01-308-5672) M100 A/P Feeder System: 3-Phase, 100 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/2; Drawing 13229E6351) (NSN 6150-01-308-5671) M40 A/P Distribution System: 3-Phase, 40 Amperes/Phase (MIL-DTL-53126/3; Drawing 13229E6353) (NSN 6150-01-307-9446) M46 Utility Assembly: Electrical Receptacles and Illumination Kit (MIL-DTL-53126/5; Drawing 13226E7046) (NSN 6150-01-208-9751) Procurement Baseline: Build-to-print execution using existing Government TDPs, MIL-DTL-53126, and associated specification slash sheets. TDPs for the PDISE systems are available upon request. 3.0 PURPOSE OF THIS RFI The Government seeks to determine: The availability of qualified large and small business sources under NAICS 335999 and 335313 capable of manufacturing, testing, and delivering the PDISE family of systems. Industry capacity and lead times for manufacturing and assembling heavy-duty electrical power-distribution equipment, including Class L connectors, ruggedized cables, military packaging and specialized circuit breakers. Vendor capability to conduct First Article Testing (FAT) and environmental testing per MIL-DTL-53126. Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) unit cost for each item. The feasibility of small business set-asides (e.g., Total Small Business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, or WOSB). 4.0 SPECIFIC INFORMATION REQUESTED (VENDOR QUESTIONNAIRE) Interested vendors are requested to provide clear, detailed responses to the questions below. Generic corporate marketing brochures that do not directly address these technical and manufacturing questions will not be considered. Section A: Corporate & Business Information Company Profile: Provide Company History (years in business), Name, Address, Website, CAGE Code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) under SAM.gov. Business Size Standards: State your business size (number of employees) and socio-economic status under NAICS 335999 and 335313. Specify if your firm is: Large Business Small Business (SB) Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB) / 8(a) Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone) Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB / EDWOSB) Role & Teaming Intent: Do you intend to respond to a solicitation as a Prime Contractor, Joint Venture / Teaming Partner, or Subcontractor? If teaming or subcontracting, describe proposed workshare allocations and your strategy to satisfy the Limitations on Subcontracting (FAR 52.219-14). Workload: If your company is awarded the contract, will you be able to perform at least 50% (percent) of the work required in house? Relevant Corporate Experience and Past Performance: Provide up to three examples of recent, relevant efforts involving build-to-print manufacture, inspection, testing, and delivery of ruggedized electrical distribution equipment, cable assemblies, or comparable military hardware. For each example, identify the customer, period of performance, scope, quantities, contract value, and customer point of contact, if available. Limit each past-performance example to two pages. Section B: Build-to-Print Manufacturing & Technical Capabilities TDP & Specification Conformance: PDISE requires fabrication to Government TDPs without redesign. Describe your facility�s experience manufacturing ruggedized power distribution centers, electrical enclosures, and high-power tactical cables to Government drawings (ASME Y14.100 / MIL-STD-31000). Tooling & Production Processes: Describe your capabilities for: Heavy-gauge multi-conductor power cable assembly. Assembly and wiring of circuit breaker inside distribution enclosures. Integration of MIL-DTL-22992 (Class L) heavy-duty cylindrical connectors into enclosures and cabling. Facilities and Production Control: Describe the availability, size, and location of facilities; manufacturing equipment; production capacity; production-control processes; records-management practices; and reporting systems used to support cost, schedule, and performance requirements. Chemical Agent Resistant Coating (CARC): PDISE enclosures require pre-treatment and painting conforming to MIL-DTL-53072 and SAE-AMS-STD-595. Does your facility possess in-house CARC painting capabilities or do you rely on qualified third-party coating vendors? Packaging & Wood Packaging Material (WPM): Can your facility provide military preservation, marking, and crating conforming to Drawings 13230E7021/7020/7019? Manufacturing Readiness Level (MRL): What is your current assessed Manufacturing Readiness Level for this class of tactical electrical distribution hardware? In-Process and Final Inspection: Describe your processes for receiving inspection of components and materials, in-process inspection, final inspection, nonconformance control, and documentation of inspection of completed PDISE or similar end items, as applicable. Section C: First Article Testing (FAT) & Environmental Qualification In-House vs. Subcontracted Testing: PDISE First Article Preproduction Inspection (FAT) requires 2 units per configuration tested within 180�360 Days After Contract Award (DACA). Identify whether your company possesses internal testing facilities or an established relationship with a DoD-certified laboratory to conduct First Article Testing in accordance with MIL-DTL-53126. Failure Escalation & Root Cause Analysis: Describe your engineering experience and/or procedures for performing root cause failure investigations and delivering Failed Item Analysis Reports (FIARs) and

title: FUEL SERVICES AND OPERATIONS SUPPORT IN WEST OHAU, HAWAII
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION SPE603-26-R-5X69 FUEL SERVICES AND OPERATIONS SUPPORT IN WEST OAHU, HAWAII Defense Logistics Agency Energy is seeking information on industry capabilities/interest/potential sources for the receipt, storage, additive injection, and shipment of U.S. Government-owned Aviation Turbine Fuel Grades Jet-A, JP-5 and Naval Distillate Fuel Grade F-76 in West Oahu, Hawaii. This announcement constitutes a Request for Information (RFI) only; there is no solicitation at this time. The Government is neither negotiating nor calling for offers at this time. This announcement is an expression of interest only and does not commit the Government to pay for any response preparation cost. The Government will not make an award on the basis of this RFI. CONCEPT OF SERVICES OPERATIONS: Fuel storage and services would primarily consist of receipt, storage, additive injection, and shipment of U.S. Government-owned Jet-A, JP-5 and F-76. All storage, services, and capabilities must be available and operational at a single location. AREA OF CONSIDERATION: West Oahu, HI ESTIMATED ANNUAL THROUGHPUT: 3,500,000 barrels of total throughput for each 12-month contract period. CAPABILITIES SOUGHT: Storage of Aviation Turbine Fuel, Grades Jet-A, JP-5 and Naval Distillate Fuel F-76 totaling 1,500,000 barrels. All fuel must be stored at a single location. Receiving capability via Tanker/Barge and Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam (JBPHH)/Red Hill (RH) tank farm and commercial/refinery pipeline, additive injection, and shipping capability via Tanker/Barge, pipeline to JBPHH, and tank truck. The facility must be equipped with illumination to allow receipt and shipping operations during hours of darkness. Submissions should be sent to Claude.Johnson@dla.mil NLT 3:00 P.M. local Fort Belvoir, VA time on August 21, 2026. Please direct any questions concerning this RFI to Contract Specialist, Claude Johnson at Claude.Johnson@dla.mil or (445) 737-8439, and/or Contracting Officer, Mark A. Laskoski at Mark.Laskoski@dla.mil or (717) 831-6975. Interested firms must include in their submission, the RFI number SPE603-26-R-5X69 in the subject line of their emails. The following information is requested: 1. Provide a company profile to include number of employees, annual revenue history (last 3 years), office location(s), DUNS/CAGE Code number, business size, and a statement regarding current business status. 2. Capability Statement. Provide a brief explanation of your firm's capabilities to provide Contractor-Owned, Contractor-Operated Fuel Storage Facilities, equipment, tools, materials, supplies, and supervision necessary to receive, store, issue, maintain quality, account for petroleum products, maintain the associated fuel facilities and to provide qualified and experienced personnel, with appropriate clearances, if required. 3. Past Performance. Do you have past performance as a prime contractor or subcontractor on a service contract for similar fuels management requirements? If so, please provide the following information: Contract number, Name of Government Agency or Commercial Entity, Period of Performance, Dollar Value, Type of Contract (Fixed Price, Cost Reimbursement, etc.), and an explanation of services provided as they relate to COCO fuels management. If your firm acted as a subcontractor or joint venture, name the prime contractor or other party, the specific work performed and percentage. Address any past performance problems, and resolutions taken. 4. Location: Please provide the location/address of your facility.
