title: FUEL SERVICES AND OPERATIONS SUPPORT IN WEST OHAU, HAWAII
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION SPE603-26-R-5X69 FUEL SERVICES AND OPERATIONS SUPPORT IN WEST OAHU, HAWAII Defense Logistics Agency Energy is seeking information on industry capabilities/interest/potential sources for the receipt, storage, additive injection, and shipment of U.S. Government-owned Aviation Turbine Fuel Grades Jet-A, JP-5 and Naval Distillate Fuel Grade F-76 in West Oahu, Hawaii. This announcement constitutes a Request for Information (RFI) only; there is no solicitation at this time. The Government is neither negotiating nor calling for offers at this time. This announcement is an expression of interest only and does not commit the Government to pay for any response preparation cost. The Government will not make an award on the basis of this RFI. CONCEPT OF SERVICES OPERATIONS: Fuel storage and services would primarily consist of receipt, storage, additive injection, and shipment of U.S. Government-owned Jet-A, JP-5 and F-76. All storage, services, and capabilities must be available and operational at a single location. AREA OF CONSIDERATION: West Oahu, HI ESTIMATED ANNUAL THROUGHPUT: 3,500,000 barrels of total throughput for each 12-month contract period. CAPABILITIES SOUGHT: Storage of Aviation Turbine Fuel, Grades Jet-A, JP-5 and Naval Distillate Fuel F-76 totaling 2,051,000 barrels. All fuel must be stored at a single location. Receiving capability via Tanker/Barge and Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam (JBPHH)/Red Hill (RH) tank farm and commercial/refinery pipeline, additive injection, and shipping capability via Tanker/Barge, pipeline to JBPHH, and tank truck. The facility must be equipped with illumination to allow receipt and shipping operations during hours of darkness. Submissions should be sent to Claude.Johnson@dla.mil NLT 3:00 P.M. local Fort Belvoir, VA time on October 22, 2026. Please direct any questions concerning this RFI to Contract Specialist, Claude Johnson at Claude.Johnson@dla.mil or (445) 737-8439, and/or Contracting Officer, Mark A. Laskoski at Mark.Laskoski@dla.mil or (717) 831-6975. Interested firms must include in their submission, the RFI number SPE603-26-R-5X69 in the subject line of their emails. The following information is requested: 1. Provide a company profile to include number of employees, annual revenue history (last 3 years), office location(s), DUNS/CAGE Code number, business size, and a statement regarding current business status. 2. Capability Statement. Provide a brief explanation of your firm's capabilities to provide Contractor-Owned, Contractor-Operated Fuel Storage Facilities, equipment, tools, materials, supplies, and supervision necessary to receive, store, issue, maintain quality, account for petroleum products, maintain the associated fuel facilities and to provide qualified and experienced personnel, with appropriate clearances, if required. 3. Past Performance. Do you have past performance as a prime contractor or subcontractor on a service contract for similar fuels management requirements? If so, please provide the following information: Contract number, Name of Government Agency or Commercial Entity, Period of Performance, Dollar Value, Type of Contract (Fixed Price, Cost Reimbursement, etc.), and an explanation of services provided as they relate to COCO fuels management. If your firm acted as a subcontractor or joint venture, name the prime contractor or other party, the specific work performed and percentage. Address any past performance problems, and resolutions taken. 4. Location: Please provide the location/address of your facility.

title: Survival Vest Improvement System
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT ONLY. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary, and the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government. The Naval Air Warfare Center, Aircraft Division (NAWCAD), Patuxent River, Maryland is requesting information and conducting market research to identify and determine if there are potential sources to manufacture and deliver a Survival Vest Improvement System (SVSI). SVSI is comprised of a new survival vest, VIPER, and a low-profile Life Preserver Unit, Serpent. VIPER is a NAVAIR owned design that incorporates a Small Business Innovative Research (SBIR) armor release system designed by Bunker Supply. The LPU Technical Data Package is owned by Switlik Parachute Company. As part of its market research, NAVAIR - PMA202 is issuing this Sources Sought to determine if there exist an adequate number of qualified interested contractors capable of providing the requirement. The Government may use the responses to this Sources Sought for information and planning purposes. This Sources Sought is only for the purpose of identifying potential sources as part of NAVAIR � PMA202 market research. No Request For Quote (RFQ) exists; therefore, do not request a copy of the RFQ. Responses to this Sources Sought are not quotes on which the NAVAIR � PMA202 can issue any contract. This Sources Sought is issued for information and planning purposes only and does not itself constitute an RFP or RFQ. The Government does not intend to award a contract vehicle based only on responses to this Sources Sought. All information received in response to this Sources Sought marked "Proprietary" will be protected and handled accordingly. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition sensitive information contained in their response. Responses to the Sources Sought will not be returned. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this Sources Sought. NAVAIR � PMA202 will not pay for information received in response to this Sources Sought. Do not submit pricing information in response to this Sources Sought. Interested sources shall provide a response detailing their capability to manufacture and deliver SVSI. Respondents should provide a brief description of their experience manufacturing similar equipment, including any relevant past performance data (if available). Additionally, respondents should include their experience with manufacturing Critical Safety Items. Respondents should also describe their capacity; production quantities are anticipated between 260 and 1543 annually with the potential to go higher . The Government anticipates a solicitation for a five-year Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) in Fiscal Year 2027. The Government will provide a TDP with the solicitation in FY27 for the vest. The government does not possess or own data rights necessary to distribute for the LPU. Any interested parties MUST copy all parties listed below: Greg Tollefsen, Procurement Contracting Officer gregory.e.tollefsen.civ@us.navy.mil Amy Wescott, Contract Specialist amy.l.wescott.civ@us.navy.mil No telephonic responses WILL NOT be accepted.

title: Commercial Vehicle Rental Services for 2027 Tinker AFB Airshow
description: This is a Sources Sought notice for market research purposes only. This is not a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of qualified businesses to provide commercial vehicle rental services for the Tinker Air Force Base (AFB) Airshow, scheduled for June 2027. The Government is seeking to identify sources that are capable of providing the required vehicles and services as detailed in the Performance Work Statement (PWS) excerpts below. RFO Part 32 Notice to Offeror(s)/Supplier(s): "Funds are not presently available for this effort. No award will be made under any future solicitation until funds are available. The Government reserves the right to cancel any future solicitation, either before or after the closing date. In the event the Government cancels the solicitation, the Government has no obligation to reimburse an offeror for any costs." 3. Background The 72nd Logistics Readiness Squadron (72 LRS) at Tinker AFB requires a short-term, commercial vehicle rental contract to support performer, dignitary, and mission-essential staff transportation during the upcoming airshow, scheduled for 5-6 June 2027. The objective is to secure a turnkey, Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) vehicle fleet with zero financial or physical liability to the United States Government. 4. Summary of Requirements The contractor shall provide all commercial vehicles, comprehensive zero-deductible insurance, routine maintenance, on-site logistics, and administrative management. Key requirements include: Fleet Composition (Estimated 86 Vehicles): 59 Compact/Mid-Size Sedans (e.g., Ford Focus, Toyota Camry) 26 Multi-Passenger Vans (e.g., Dodge Grand Caravan, Ford Transit) 1 Light-Duty Pickup Truck (e.g., Ford F-150, Ram 1500) Vehicle Standards: All vehicles must be late model (2023 or newer), clean, delivered with a full tank of fuel, and in prime operational condition. Zero-Liability Model: The contract will require comprehensive, zero-deductible Loss/Collision Damage Waivers (LDW/CDW) and prohibit any post-rental claims for damage, loss, or wear-and-tear. Delivery & Logistics: The entire fleet must be delivered to a designated staging area on Tinker AFB via commercial multi-car haulers on 3 June 2027 and retrieved on 8 June 2027. All transport personnel must comply with base access and security vetting. Driver Authorization: The contractor must agree to a broad driver authorization clause covering any licensed military member, DoD civilian, or authorized performer without requiring individual driver add-ons or surcharges. Administrative Compliance: Vendors must have an active SAM.gov registration (NAICS 532111) and be capable of submitting invoices electronically via Wide Area Workflow (WAWF). 5. Information Requested from Interested Parties Interested parties are requested to submit a response that includes: Vendor Profile: Legal Company Name Point of Contact (Name, Title, Email, Phone) CAGE Code and Unique Entity ID (UEI) Business Size/Socioeconomic Status (e.g., Small, SDVOSB, WOSB, Large) Capability Statement: A brief statement (not to exceed 5 pages) describing your company's ability to meet the requirements outlined above. Please specifically address your ability to provide the specified fleet quantity and adhere to the zero-liability, insurance, and on-base delivery requirements. Completed Questionnaire: Please complete and return the attached "Tinker AFB Airshow Vehicle Rental Questionnaire." Feedback (Optional): Any questions or feedback regarding the requirements or the Draft PWS that would help clarify the Government's needs. 6. Response Submission Please submit your responses via email to the point of contact listed below by [Insert Response Date and Time]. Primary Point of Contact: Name: Mario Tedeschi Organization: AFSC/PZIOA, Tinker AFB Email: mario_cassiel.tedeschi@us.af.mil Primary Point of Contact: Name: Michael Shand Organization: AFSC/PZIOA, Tinker AFB Email: michael.shand@us.af.mil 7. Disclaimer The Government does not intend to award a contract on the basis of this notice or to otherwise pay for the information solicited. This notice is for informational and planning purposes and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government. The information provided may be used by the Air Force in developing its acquisition strategy and statement of work.

title: Nationwide Support to Marine Forces Reserve in Disposing of Hazardous and Nonhazardous Waste and Provision of Environmental Compliance Services
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This is not a request for proposal and no contract will be awarded from this notice. There will not be a solicitation, specifications, or drawings available at this time. This notice is a market research tool used for planning purposes only to determine the availability and capability of businesses. Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Mid-Atlantic (NAVFAC MIDLANT) is seeking Large Business, Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Women Owned Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business, certified HUBZone Small Business, certified 8(a) Businesses with current relevant qualifications, experience, personnel and capability are encouraged to respond. Upon review of industry response to this Sources Sought Notice, the Government will determine whether a set-aside acquisition in lieu of full and open competition is in the best interest of the Government. A Firm-Fixed Price/Indefinite Quantity type, performance-based contract is anticipated. The total contract term including the exercise of any options, shall not exceed 60 months. Source Selection procedures will be used to evaluate and select the proposal that is most advantageous to the Government. The Contractor shall provide all labor, management, supervision, tools, materials, transportation, and equipment required to perform environmental services and regulated waste collection and disposal at Marine Forces Reserve (MARFORRES) facilities located in 48 states (all states not including Alaska and Hawaii), Puerto Rico and the District of Columbia and at Naval Reserve Centers and Navy installations within the Naval Facilities Engineering Command Mid-Atlantic Area of Responsibility including the following states: Connecticut, Delaware, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, Vermont, Virginia, West Virginia, and Wisconsin. General Work Requirements: The contractor shall provide environmental services that include, but are not limited to: Coordinate and schedule the collection and disposal of hazardous and non-hazardous, universal waste, potentially infectious medical wastes and sharps, used tires, scrap metal / bulk debris, electronic waste, and other regulated wastes. Provide and manage a customer accessible, web-based system for all disposal record, waste characterization information, disposal facility audits and related data and information. Recycle, to the maximum extent possible, including (but not limited to): used oil, used anti-freeze, batteries and other recyclable materials and universal wastes. Perform on-site waste stream characterization, waste profiling, hazardous and other regulated waste compliance tracking, recordkeeping and reporting. Provide pollution prevention materials (drums, absorbents, spill kits, etc.) and equipment to government facilities. Perform sampling and laboratory analysis of waste materials, building components, drinking water, and environmental conditions in soil, wastewater and surface water. Provide on-site solvent and aqueous parts washer services. Provide oil water separator inspection, cleaning and pump out, maintenance and repair services. Perform petroleum storage tank inspections, cleaning, pump-out, maintenance and repair services. Perform radon facility testing, and maintenance and repair of radon ventilation mitigation systems. Perform maintenance and repair of hazardous material and regulated waste facilities, storage lockers and equipment and associated fire suppression and alarm systems. Perform surveys of facilities for environmental contaminants, including lead paint, asbestos, mercury containing devices, PCB-containing electrical components, mold, low level radiological materials and historical record (EDR) searches. Perform cleanup of environmental contaminant spills. Inspect compressed gas cylinders and determine compliance with DOT hydro-testing, certification and suitability for transportation. Perform lab packing and consolidation and co-mingling of on-site wastes. Perform on-site site waste cleanout activities, including: characterizing and containerizing on-site hazardous materials and regulated wastes, performing sampling and laboratory analysis to determine characteristics and constituents of wastes, packaging and labeling and marking drums, cylinders, and other containers; performing pressure washing and steam cleaning of stained pavements and drains and sewers, pumping out and cleaning storage tanks and lubrication systems and oil water separators. Perform tracking and management of service deliveries, manifests and disposal records; assist in preparation of regulatory required recordkeeping and reporting; tabulate monthly waste and service delivery metrics and costs. Provide oily shop rag recycling / exchange service on a monthly basis. Perform maintenance and installation of storm water management best management practices, including replacement of silt fencing, cleanout sediment from storm inlets, sewers, and structures, and physically remove and dispose of accumulated sediment, debris and vegetation in drainageways. Perform the recovery and disposal of refrigerants from facility HVAC systems and government refrigeration and cooling equipment. Typical regulated waste and hazardous materials managed under this contract includes but not limited to: Used oil; and water contaminated with used oil Waste fuels, gasoline, diesel, heating oil, and others Used antifreeze/coolants and off spec coolants Used oil contaminated absorbents, filters and debris Waste oil and waste oil sludges Used absorbents and rags contaminated with oils and fuels Used lead acid batteries Lithium ion, polymer, metal hydride, manganese and sulfur dioxide batteries Alkaline batteries Waste paint related materials in aerosol cans, caulk tubes, quart, gallon, and larger containers Contaminated coolants - ethylene and propylene glycol (potentially contaminated with water, oil, brake fluid, and fuels) Oily bilge water (>95% water, containing oil, antifreeze, fuel contaminants) - Galveston TX, Gulfport MS, Jacksonville FL, Norfolk VA (Little Creek), Tampa FL, Syracuse, NY and other facilities. Soil and sediments contaminated with fuels, petroleum and lubricants Medical potentially infectious waste, expired vaccines and medications, and used sharps Compressed gas cylinders, empty and containing: inert gases, oxidizers, refrigerants, fire extinguishers, and flammable gases, including over packed leaking cylinders Waste consumer products containing surfactants, oxidizers, corrosives, solvents, and others Corrosive acid and bases Off-specification and expired shelf-life oils, fuels, coolants and other products Used lamps, fluorescent, LED bulbs, aerosol paints, and other universal wastes Lab packing small containers of paint related materials, consumer products, cleaners, and other materials, including labor effort and technician support All Large Business, Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Women Owned Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business, certified HUBZone Small Business, and certified 8(a) Businesses are encouraged to respond. The Government will not pay for any information solicited. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. All qualified firms are encouraged to respond. The appropriate NAICS Code is 562211. It is requested that interested parties submit a brief capabilities package not to exceed 10 pages. This capabilities package shall address, at a minimum the following: 1. Examples of projects worked within the last five years of similar size, scope and complexity as the work indicated. Knowledge of the Federal and State environmental regulations within the AOR. Indicate whether your firm worked as a prime or subcontractor, contract value, brief description and tabular depiction of how the referenced contract relates to the work

Work will include but not be limited to topographic surveying, property/boundary surveys, geodetic control surveys, remote sensing surveys, construction surveys, inland hydrographic surveying, and near-shore hydrographic surveying. The primary purpose of this proposed contract is to provide services for projects located within that portion of the State of Florida that resides in the geographic boundaries of the Jacksonville District area of responsibility. The anticipated contract will be an Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity contract for a period of one year from date of award, with options to extend up to four additional years; not to exceed a total of five years. description: Naval Air System Command (NAVAIR), PMX-280 Tactical Tomahawk, Patuxent River, MD, intends to negotiate and award a sole-source Contract for the Low-Rate Initial Production (LRIP) of the Joint Multiple Effects Warhead System (JMEWS) to Raytheon Company, (Raytheon) Tucson, AZ 85756-9367. Since 1994, RMD has been the sole developer, designer, and manufacturer for the Tomahawk missile. PROJECT OVERVIEWS The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), in support of the United States Air Force (USAF), is conducting market research to identify interested and qualified industry partners for the design and construction of several upcoming construction projects at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB), Ohio. PROJECT 1: RENOVATE NASIC MAIN CAMPUS, PHASE 1, F/10853 - This project is renovation of 170,000 SF of Sensitive and/or Special Access Program spaces. The work consists of the full renovation of F/10853 through reconfiguration and interior renovation to create a network of administrative functions. The work shall be done in accordance with Intelligence Community Directive 705 (ICD 705) criteria and standards. The interior demolition consists of removal of all architectural and mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) elements including floor, wall, and ceiling finishes. Work includes replacement of building systems, reconfiguration of interior partitions, life safety systems, roof replacement, and envelope modification. The roofing system will be replaced with an energy-compliant system. Penetrations will be added to the building for daylighting, and the exterior envelope will be modified on first floor locations for mechanical rooms. All piping and sprinklers that are part of the current fire protection system are to be replaced. All domestic water, storm, and sanitary piping will be replaced. Additionally, this project includes cybersecurity measures. A corridor bridge connecting F/10828 and F/10856 over an existing loading dock is to be constructed. Personnel will require swing space during the renovation of F/10853. Swing space will be provided through existing available spaces throughout the NASIC IPC campus or via a temporary facility. It is critical that the sequencing of repair work be considered so that available spaces are not overwhelmed. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: Approximately $160,000,000 PROJECT 2: Advanced Materials Research Laboratory � C2A - Construction of an approximately ~90,000 SF three-story laboratory and research facility, as well as the potential construction of a central utility plant for the Air Force Reach Labor Material and Manufacturing Directorate. New facility will consist of concrete, foundation, structural steel frame, masonry etc. Onsite gas boilers for heat and chilled water generation for cooling and lab processes. The interior shall consist of open inter-disciplinary collaboration labs with clean utilities, vibration isolation, precision HVAC and humidity controls, as well as fire protection/suppression, intrusion detections systems and medium voltage switchgear (i.e. 12,470 volts). Site work consists of utilities, sidewalks, parking, communications The new facility shall connect to existing facilities and demolitions of facility 20654. is part of this project. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: Approximately $122,000,000 PROJECT 3: Compressor Research Facility Systems Modernization This project will modernize the Air Force Research Lab�s (AFRL) Compressor Research Facility (CRF) by replacing legacy drive and power equipment with a new 30,000-horsepower Variable Frequency Drive system to support engine component testing. The effort will deliver a fully integrated system that improves reliability, control, maintainability, and long-term test capability. Work includes replacement of the existing drive system with a new 30,000-horsepower VFD with active front end, a new 30,000-horsepower brushless synchronous motor, a new primary transformer, medium-voltage switchgear, protective relaying, and all associated interconnecting cables, bus work, grounding, and terminations. The project also includes the demolition and removal of legacy electrical and mechanical equipment; upgrades to controls, monitoring interfaces, cooling and ventilation systems, and supporting electrical infrastructure; and any required structural, foundation, enclosure, or fire/life-safety modifications needed to install and operate the new equipment. Additional work will include system integration, testing, commissioning, performance verification, operator and maintainer training, and delivery of technical data, recommended spare parts, and warranty support. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $25,000,000 PROJECT 4: Consolidate/Demo F/31240 This project will decentralize Area A heating by replacing the aging high-temperature hot water (HTHW) system fed from Building F/31240, Line A, and Line D with standalone boiler plants serving 49 facilities. The project supports administrative, warehouse, laboratory, hangar, and dormitory buildings that require year-round hot water for heating, reheating, humidity control, and climate management. Work includes facility surveys, evaluation of mechanical room capacity and code compliance, and determination of any needed interior renovations or limited additions to support the new equipment. The project also includes demolition of Building F/31240 and its boiler equipment, removal of above-ground HTHW piping and supports, and capping and abandonment of below-grade piping in place. New high-efficiency boiler systems, pumps, controls, and related accessories will be installed at affected facilities, with evaluation of both natural gas-fired and electric options. Additional work includes mechanical room modifications, make-up water assemblies where needed, upgrades to electrical, fire alarm, fire suppression, and direct digital control systems, and site restoration including pavement repair, grass restoration, and backfill and seeding at the demolished plant site. Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $66,500,000 PROJECT 5: Consolidate/Demo West Ramp This project will decentralize heating for the West Ramp area at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base by replacing the existing high-temperature hot water (HTHW) system from Building F/34019 with standalone boiler plants serving 15 surrounding facilities. The effort addresses aging and degraded infrastructure supporting administrative, laboratory, and active hangar facilities that require year-round hot water for comfort heating, reheating, humidity control, and climate management. The project includes surveying each facility to determine boiler locations, evaluating mechanical room walls for code compliance, and assessing whether mechanical room expansions, electrical upgrades, or system improvements are needed to support the new equipment. Work includes demolition and removal of Building F/34019 and its internal boiler equipment, along with demolition of the exterior emergency generator, tank, piping, and all above-ground HTHW piping, supports, and foundations. Below-grade piping will be capped and abandoned in place. Each affected facility will receive new high-efficiency boiler systems, distribution pumps, controls, and related accessories, with evaluation of both natural gas-fired and electric boiler options. REQUIREMENTS GENERAL REQUIREMENTS: The Contractor shall provide at the contractors facility the necessary repair labor, new and serviceable reworked repair parts, materials and test equipmentand arrange for outside services as required to return the equipment to a serviceable condition within the calendar day shop time as specified in the delivery schedule of the contract. SCOPE OF WORK FOR REPAIR: The scope of the work in the following subparagraphs are applicable to the latest configuration of the Government equipment.There shall be a 100% repair rate on all CLIN carcasses. Any carcass that cannot be repaired must have Defense Contract Mnagement Command (DCMC) Quality Assurance Representative(QAR) approval for disposal. Upon receipt of Government equipment the contractor shall perform incoming inspections, recording any shipping damage, and inventory components for completeness. Units with missing parts will not be inducted until missing partsare received or unless specifically authorized by the Procurment Contracting Officer (PCO). The contractor shall advise the PCO if any portion of the required servicing is a result of the furnishing by the contractor of articles that were defective in material and/or workmanship or otherwise not in conformance with the requirements of the contract under which such government equipment were originally furnished. In the event that the failed assembly is found to be beyond economical repair (BER), as defined in the contract, or in the event that the Government equipment is received with one or more subassemblies missing (FOR EXAMPLE: AS ARESULT OF CANNABALIZATION BY AN AIRCRAFT OPERATING SITE),the contractor shall promptly obtain confirmation of such findings from the cognizant DCMC QAR. and upon confirmation promptly notify the PCO for authority to scrap if BER and,if missing subassemblies, proceed IAW Missing on Induction (MOI).Units with missing parts will not be inducted until missing parts are received or unless specifically authorized by the PCO. All disassembly, repair and assembly of the Government equipment shall be IAW current engineering drawings and configuration specifications. All detail parts shall be inspected IAW the applicable repair specification and repaired or replaced as indicated. Replaced hardware shall be in accordance with the latest drawing revisions.The contractor shall provide and may use new or repaired/reworked parts which meet the requirements of the repair specification to restore the Government equipment in the delivery time specified in the contract. Repaired/reworked parts shall be used in lieu of new whenever possible as allowed by the applicable repair specification.Any repair of lower assemblies and/or detail parts not authorized by the by the applicable repair specification shall be submitted to the QAR for Government review and approval.Requests for repair approvals shall be accompanied by details of the repair and other applicable data such as tests which have been performed to validate the repair. Repaired Government equipment shall meet the inspection and acceptance test requirements of the applicable repair specifications. A contractor QA representative shall be required, in accordance with MIL-I-45208A, or ISO Quality standard equivalent, to witness repair,inspection, and acceptance tests Government representatives shall be notified of, and permitted to witnesssuch inspections at their discretion. The contractor shall submit repair procedures for Government approval prior to repair if those procedures deviate from the repair procedures detailed in the applicable repair specifications. Where the test specifications are found to be missing,inadequate,or behind in revision for a CLIN,the contractor shall develop and submit its own acceptance test procedures for Government approval to submission of the CLIN for Government acceptance. During the repair effort the contractor shall make no modifications to the CLIN that would prohibit future repair or require additional repair steps by other qualified sources. REPAIR PARTS: The contractor shall be responsible for identification, selection, ordering, and stocking of required piece parts to support all repairs. By definition," piece part" shall be any part or material listed in the applicable repair specification. TEST EQUIPMENT: The contractor will provide a laboratory facility equipped with instrumentation and testing capability for comprehensive functional testing of the equipment and detailed inspections of subassemblies and detailed parts. The contractor test equipment shall be designed to ensure repaired Government equipment function in full compliance with the requirementsof the applicable repair specification. All Government equipment's electrical performance and mechanical parameters shall be measured in accordance with the requirements of the applicable repair specification,with hard copy reports of all measurements available to the Government upon request. title: AN/UPX-50 Common Core Digital Interrogator (CCDI) Productionization
description: 1. INTRODUCTION THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. It is a market research tool being used to determine potential and eligible businesses capable of providing the services described herein prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a Request for Proposal. The Government is not obligated to and will not pay for any information received from potential sources because of this notice. The Naval Air Systems Command, (NAVAIR) Patuxent River, Maryland, Air Traffic Management Systems Program Office (PMA-213) intends to award a Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) order for the productionization of the AN/UPX-50 Common Core Digital Interrogator (CCDI). This includes transitioning from lab-built prototypes to units that can be produced in an electronics manufacturing environment, the development of unique CCDI test equipment and procedures, as well as integration of the CCDI into existing DI test equipment to ensure the CCDI meets all specified requirements. Lastly, this effort includes Automated Switch-Over (ASO) production line development, a CCDI Re-Spin option, and a CCDI Unknown Trouble Report (TR) corrections option. The anticipated period of performance is 32 months with an estimated value of $47M. The work associated with this requirement is expected to be performed at the contractor�s facilities within the United States. No work at Government sites is anticipated. The specific place(s) of performance will be determined based on the location of the contractor selected for any resulting contract. 2.0 BACKGROUND Production of AN/UPX-50(C) DI systems is currently performed on the N00019-23-C-0046 contract by BAE Systems, Information and Electronic Systems Integration. The existing contract is a Firm Fixed Price type. The AN/UPX-50(C) is a DI for ground-based shipboard weapon system platforms to satisfy Mark XIIA IFF and Mode S requirements. Technical refresh of the AN/UPX-50(C) DI system to the CCDI system is currently performed on the N0001922G0009 N0001923F0023 Cost Plus Fixed Fee BOA Order. The technical refresh effort includes the redesign of the AN/UPX-50(C) DI assemblies to resolve parts obsolescence and implement solutions to achieve compliance with the latest specifications, qualification, and certification standards. 3.0 REQUIRED CAPABILITIES Supplies and services to be procured will support the Navy�s requirement of AN/UPX 50 CCDI EDMs beginning in December 2027 to support production deliveries in December 2030 to active new ship production lines including:CVN, DDG, LHA, LHD, LPD, WMSL, and WMSM ship classes. These efforts require highly specialized skills and knowledge of the CCDI system design and engineering details to meet the stringent schedule. Productionization of the CCDI includes integration of highly complex Contractor developed algorithms in conjunction with Government cooperation using organically developed algorithms for target processing. This system is specialized for operation with the Aegis Weapon System (AWS) and Ship�s Self Defense System (SSDS), involving characterization of the system of systems in their operational environment to ensure ship requirements are met. This effort is intended to complete Non-Recurring Engineering activities, which are already in progress. Productionization will include the development and integration of highly specialized test equipment to ensure equipment meets all specified requirements. BAE Systems is the sole designer, developer and manufacturer of DI and has been the only entity producing the AN/UPX-50(C) DI for over 10 years. BAE Systems retains the Technical Data Package (TDP). Interested parties must include a detailed explanation of how they would complete the CCDI Productionization requirements without a Government furnished TDP. Responses must also explain how they would accomplish the CCDI productionization effort and provide a timeline including major milestones to support BAE Systems� CCDI production delivery requirements beginning in December 2030. This would include ensuring the offered productionized CCDI design is completed and is AIMS 17-1000 Rev 1 Box certified, including integration of internal target processing that meets the existing Combat System performance required by AWS and SSDS (in accordance with all applicable Weapon Specifications). 4.0 INCUMBENT This is a follow-on requirement. The Original Equipment Manufacturer is BAE Systems, Information and Electronic Systems Integration, 450 Pulaski Rd. Greenlawn, NY 11740USA. 5.0 ELIGIBILITY The Product and Service Code for this requirement is 5840. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 334511 (Search, Detection, Navigation, Guidance, Aeronautical, and Nautical System and Instrument Manufacturing), with a small business size standard of 1,350 employees as defined by the U.S. Small Business Administration. The Government currently anticipates a sole-source award under FAR 6.103-1 to BAE Systems due to the Government�s lack of required technical data and data rights for the AN/UPX-50 DI designs. However, all responsible sources, including small business (8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, WOSB) are encouraged to submit capability statements describing their ability to perform as a prime or subcontractor and to identify any specific portions of the requirement they can perform. All interested contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management government website at www.sam.gov to be eligible for award of Government contracts. Only interested firms who possess the supplies and services provided in this notice and can meet these requirements are invited to respond. The Government will not reimburse participants for any expenses associated with their participation in this notice. 6.0 SUBMITTAL INFORMATION It is requested that interested vendors submit to the point of contract below, a brief capabilities statement package (no more than 10 - 8.5 x 11 pages in length, single-spaced, 12-point font minimum) demonstrating the capability to meet the requirements of this notice. This documentation must address, at a minimum, the following: A company profile to include: Company name, business size under NAICS Code 334511, office location(s), Point of Contact name, phone number, email address, Commercial and Government Entity code, and Unique Entity ID. Include a brief description of any applicable contracts relating to the supplies and/or services described herein. Prior/current industry experience of similar size and scope as referenced in section 3.0 �Required Capabilities�. Address the proposed management approach to staffing the effort with qualified personnel. Include corporate management policies, quality certifications, and the experience level of currently employed personnel to be assigned tasks under this effort. Provide documentation of the company's ability to begin performance immediately upon contract award projected in December 2026, to include a detailed plan and estimated schedule(s) of performance. Include any deviation or impact, if applicable. Any anticipated schedule, cost, or technical risks associated with performing this effort as a non-OEM source, and proposed mitigations. Provide documentation to show the company's ability to meet the Required Capabilities and Eligibility of this notice to include: Whether your company possesses, or can obtain access to the technical data, software documentation, and data rights necessary to perform this effort or describe an alternative technical approach that meets all interface, performance, qualification, and certification requirements without access to OEM proprietary information. Responses shall not contain classified information. If a response includes proprietary information, it shall be clearly marked as such. The Government will handle all proprietary information in accordance with applicable law and regulations and will not disclose it outside the Government without prior permission. title: Limited Source Delivery Order for Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) Intelligence, Surveillance and Reconnaissance (ISR) Services under existing Basic Ordering Agreements � Order 3
description: The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIRSYSCOM) on behalf of the Aircraft Program Management Office (AIR PMO), acting under the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Robotic and Autonomous Systems (PAE RAS) at Patuxent River, MD, intends to compete and award a limited source Firm Fixed Price (FFP) type Delivery Order. This order will be competed under one of four existing Basic Ordering Agreements (BOAs) to the below vendors for the procurement of Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) Maritime Services: N0001925G1000: Insitu, Inc. (Insitu), East Columbia Way, Bingen, WA N0001926G1005: AeroVironment (AV), 900 Innovators Way, Simi Valley, CA N0001926G1006: Shield AI (Shield), 600 West Broadway, San Diego, CA N0001926G1007: Textron Systems (Textron), 124 Industry Lane, Hunt Valley, MD The delivery order will secure contractor-owned, contractor-operated UAS ISR services utilizing Maritime B-kits #7-#9 in support of multiple combatant commands. Contractors will be responsible for resources to produce sensor data, such as trained personnel, non-developmental UAS equipment, shipboard operations and logistics Conex containers, certifications, operation and maintenance, SpaceX Starshield SATCOM-capable hardware, spares, and product support. Contracted services would be in direct support of ISR missions requiring around-the-clock imagery and other sensor capability in support of those missions. It is anticipated that these services will support domestic and coalition military partners in combat and contingency operations based on Joint Urgent Operational Needs (JUONs), Fleet Top Level Requirements (TLR), and other operational requirements documents. The total period of performance includes a base period and four (4) option periods (to include environmental shock testing and training options) for up to 60 months of service. THIS NOTICE IS PUBLISHED FOR INFORMATION PURPOSES ONLY AND IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. A determination by the Government to compete this procurement under the existing BOA, regardless of responses to this notice, is solely within the discretion of the Government. The Government will not pay for any responses received. title: Denmark – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Udbud af WMS til nyt Lager- & Logistikcenter til Esbjerg Sygehus
description: Region Syddanmark udbyder en kontrakt vedrørende Warehouse Management System (WMS) til det nye Lager- & Logistikcenter Esbjerg Sygehus. Esbjerg Sygehus’ fysiske rammer for Depot & Forsyningstjenesten er 100% udnyttet og kan ikke understøtte den ønskede vækst og fremtidssikring, som det kræves. Depot & Forsyningstjenesten holder til i kælderetagen på Esbjerg Sygehus i dag, hvor alle varer bliver leveret på Østergade i indre by af Esbjerg. Esbjerg Sygehus nye Lager- & Logistikcenter vil danne rammerne for en øgning af varer på lageret som sikre forsyningen til Esbjerg Sygehus og samarbejdspartnere. Øgningen af lagervarer giver et positivt aftryk på den grønne omstilling i form af reduktion i transporter til Lager- & Logistikcenteret i forhold til den nuværende belastning. Den tunge og sorte trafik i Esbjerg indre by vil blive reduceret væsentlig ved etablering af Esbjerg Sygehus’ nye Lager- & Logistikcenter. Esbjerg Sygehus Lager- & Logistikcenter forsyner Esbjerg & Grindsted Sygehus, Veneklinikken i Brørup, Psykiatrien på Gl. Vardevej og alle de lokale Psykiatri afdelinger. Esbjerg Sygehus har samarbejde med de omkringliggende kommuner vedr. blandt andet IV behandlinger i borgernes eget hjem samt de kommende Sundheds- og Omsorgs Pladser. Samarbejdet indeholder en aftale med forsyninger til lokale depoter i samarbejdskommunerne. Den udbudte opgave omfatter levering, implementering, konfiguration og tilpasning af WMS, herunder etablering af integrationer, uddannelse af superbrugere og brugere, prøver og test samt idriftsættelse, drift, support og vedligeholdelse. På tidspunktet for indgåelse af den udbudte Kontrakt er lagerbygningen under opførelse. Leverandørens ydelser omfatter tillige projektledelse og koordinering med entreprenøren – KG Hansen, dog primært med leverandøren af AutoStore og Conveyor anlæg – Element Logic. WMS-løsningen som leveres, i henhold til den udbudte Kontrakt, skal opfylde de krav til funktion, kvalitet, kapacitet m.v., som fremgår af udbudsmaterialet. Regionen har behov for op til 2 sites med 3 superbrugere og 12 brugere. Det ene site skal anvendes for Esbjerg Sygehus som en del af Leverancen, og det andet site skal kobles på for Grindsted Sygehus i løbet af kontraktperioden uden yderligere omkostninger. Grindsted Sygehus har ikke et tilsvarende WMS, men alene manuelle lagre. Opgaven er udbudt som én samlet kontrakt ud fra funktionelle, markedsmæssige og økonomiske hensyn. Kontrakten er tidsubegrænset. Kunden har et opsigelsesvarsel på 12 måneder, og Leverandøren har et opsigelsesvarsel på 24 måneder, dog tidligst til udløb 5 år efter Overtagelsesdagen.

title: Germany – Electricity, heating, solar and nuclear energy – Lieferung von elektrischer Energie Ökostrom für diverse Abnahmestellen von Trägern öffentlicher Verwaltungen im Bundesland Schleswig-Holstein
description: Gegenstand der Ausschreibung ist die Lieferung von elektrischer Energie (100 % Ökostrom) als Vollstromversorgung für die in den Vergabeunterlagen bezeichneten Abnahmestellen der Auftraggeber. Der zur Versorgung der Abnahmestellen gelieferte Strom muss zu 100 % aus erneuerbaren Energien stammen. Ökostrom im Sinne dieser Ausschreibung ist Strom, der aus erneuerbaren Energiequellen erzeugt wird. Zulässige Energiequellen sind insbesondere: Wasserkraft einschließlich Wellen-, Gezeiten-, Salzgradienten- und Strömungsenergie, Windenergie, solare Strahlungsenergie, Geothermie, Biomasse einschließlich Biogas, Deponiegas und Klärgas sowie der biologisch abbaubare Anteil von Abfällen aus Haushalten und Industrie. Soweit Strom aus Biomasse eingesetzt wird, müssen die jeweils geltenden gesetzlichen Anforderungen an die eingesetzten Energieträger sowie, soweit einschlägig, die gesetzlichen Nachhaltigkeitsanforderungen erfüllt sein. Strom aus Kernenergie sowie Strom, der aus fossilen Energieträgern, insbesondere Kohle, Erdgas oder Mineralöl, erzeugt wurde, erfüllt die Anforderungen dieser Ausschreibung nicht. Dies gilt auch für Strom aus Kraft-Wärme-Kopplungsanlagen, soweit dieser unter Einsatz fossiler Energieträger erzeugt wurde. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Die Ausschreibung umfasst insgesamt 2 Lose mit ca. 499 Abnahmestellen und einem jährlichen Gesamtverbrauch von ca. 4,3 GWh. Die Abnahmestellen der Teilnehmer wurden von der ausschreibenden Stelle auf 2 Lose verteilt. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Die tatsächlichen Verbräuche im Lieferzeitraum können nutzungsbedingt von den ermittelten Verbräuchen auf Basis der Verbrauchsdaten im Referenzjahr abweichen. Die Anzahl der Verbrauchseinrichtungen kann ebenfalls während der Vertragslaufzeit variieren. Wegen weiterer Einzelheiten wird auf die Vorbemerkungen zum Stromliefervertrag verwiesen. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Toleranzband: Für das Lieferjahr 2027 gilt für jeden Auftraggeber ein Toleranzband von ± 10 % der für diesen Auftraggeber maßgeblichen Gesamt-Referenzmenge. Die Mindestabnahmemenge zu den vereinbarten Lieferkonditionen beträgt je Auftraggeber 90 % der Gesamt-Referenzmenge des Lieferjahres 2027. Die Maximalabnahmemenge zu den vereinbarten Lieferkonditionen beträgt je Auftraggeber 110 % der Gesamt-Referenzmenge des Lieferjahres 2027. Für die Prüfung des Toleranzbandes werden die tatsächlichen Verbrauchsmengen sämtlicher im Lieferjahr 2027 zur Versorgung angemeldeter Abnahmestellen des jeweiligen Auftraggebers gemeinsam betrachtet. Soweit innerhalb eines Auftraggebers unterschiedliche Preis- oder Messgruppen bestehen, werden deren Verbrauchsmengen für die Prüfung des Toleranzbandes zusammengefasst. Verbrauchsabweichungen innerhalb des Toleranzbandes führen zu keiner gesonderten Mehr- oder Mindermengenabrechnung. Eine gesonderte Mehr- oder Mindermengenabrechnung kann ausschließlich für Verbrauchsmengen erfolgen, die außerhalb des vorstehend festgelegten Toleranzbandes liegen. Hinsichtlich der Einzelheiten der Mehr- und Mindermengenabrechnung wird auf Ziffer 10 dieser Leistungsbeschreibung verwiesen. Die Betrachtung des Toleranzbandes erfolgt für jeden Teilnehmer gesondert. Maßgeblich ist die Summe der tatsächlichen Verbrauchsmengen sämtlicher im Lieferjahr 2027 zur Versorgung angemeldeter Abnahmestellen des jeweiligen Teilnehmers im Verhältnis zu dessen Gesamt-Referenzmenge. Ein Ausgleich von Mehr- oder Minderverbräuchen zwischen verschiedenen Teilnehmern desselben Loses findet nicht statt. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Die maximal beziehbare Energiemenge beträgt für das Lieferjahr 2027 je Auftraggeber 150 % der für diesen Auftraggeber maßgeblichen Gesamt-Referenzmenge. Unabhängig hiervon beträgt die absolute Höchstmenge der im Rahmen des jeweiligen Loses insgesamt beziehbaren Energie 150 % der für das betreffende Los ausgewiesenen Gesamt-Referenzmenge. Der Mengenbereich zwischen 110 % und 150 % der jeweiligen Gesamt-Referenzmenge gehört nicht zum Toleranzband und wird nach den Regelungen zur Mehrmengenabrechnung abgerechnet. Die vorstehenden Höchstmengen stellen keine Abnahmeverpflichtung des Auftraggebers dar. Eine Verpflichtung zur Abnahme besteht ausschließlich nach Maßgabe der Regelungen zum Toleranzband und der sonstigen Vertragsbestimmungen. Mit Erreichen der für das jeweilige Los festgelegten absoluten Höchstmenge können aus der Rahmenvereinbarung keine weiteren Liefermengen zu den Bedingungen dieser Ausschreibung verlangt werden. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Pro Los wird ein Rahmenvertrag mit einem Anbieter geschlossen. Es erfolgt keine Los- oder Zuschlagslimitierung.

description: The subject of this call for tenders is the service portfolio related to the European Commission’s Digital Workplace (DWP) and its customers and users, ensuring the provision of efficient, end-user experience driven, proactive and resilient solutions and support services. The procedure aims to ensure the operational continuity while driving progress through the adoption of latest technologies aligning to the evolving business objectives of the European Commission, targeting the services falling within the scope of the current framework contract DI-07810, awarded under Lot 1 of the open call for tenders DIGIT/A3/PO/2018/015 EUSS-SM and expiring in June 2027. Komplettiert wird der vorhandene Gebäudekomplex von einer kleinen Sporthalle, deren Errichtungszeitraum, wie bei den Schulgebäuden, in die Zeit zum Ende der 1960er Jahre einzuordnen ist. Aktuell nutzen Vereine die räumlichen Kapazitäten für ihren Trainingsbetrieb. Die genauen Angaben entnehmen Sie bitte der Leistungsbeschreibung.

description: Das LZN ist als Auftraggeber und einzige abrufberechtigte Stelle zum Abschluss von Einzelaufträgen auf Grundlage dieser Rahmenvereinbarung berechtigt. Es wird zur Erfüllung seiner Aufgaben als zentraler Dienst-leister der unmittelbaren niedersächsischen Landesverwaltung sowie weiterer öffentlicher Stellen Leistungen aus dieser Rahmenvereinbarung in Anspruch nehmen. In dieser Zuständigkeit umfasst der Auftrag den Abschluss einer Rahmenvereinbarung mit einem Unterneh-men (§ 21 VgV) über die Lieferung von Gewahrsamsdecken. Die auf Grundlage dieser Rahmenvereinbarung abzuschließenden Einzelaufträge (Abrufe) werden durch und im Namen des LZN für die unmittelbare Landesverwaltung sowie für weitere öffentliche Stellen getätigt, die mit dem LZN eine Liefer- bzw. Leistungsvereinbarung geschlossen haben (bezugsberechtigte Stellen). Die hierfür erforderlichen Bedarfe sind in die Gesamtbedarfsschätzung eingeflossen. Die jeweils bezugsberechtig-ten Stellen sind alle Polizeidienststellen inkl. der niedersächsischen Inseln in Niedersachsen sowie alle Dienst-stellen der Polizei im Freistaat Thüringen. Bei jedem Abruf teilt das LZN dem Auftragnehmer die Lieferadresse sowie die für den Versand und die Anlieferung erforderlichen Kontaktdaten mit, welche einer der bezugsbe-rechtigten Stellen aus der Liste zugeordnet sind. Im gegenseitigen Einvernehmen kann die Liste der bezugsberechtigten Stellen während der gesamten Lauf-zeit der Rahmenvereinbarung mit dem Auftragnehmer in Textform um weitere öffentliche Stellen ergänzt werden, sofern die zugrunde gelegte Gesamtbedarfsschätzung hierdurch nicht überschritten wird. Die Auf-nahme weiterer bezugsberechtigter Stellen hat keine Auswirkungen auf das in Ziffer 1.5 festgelegte Maximal-volumen der Rahmenvereinbarung. Die Rechnungsstellung erfolgt ausschließlich gegenüber dem LZN als Auftraggeber und Vertragspartner. Nähere Einzelheiten zu Art und Umfang des Auftrags sind der Leistungsbeschreibung - Fachlicher Teil (Teil B) zu entnehmen.

description: Upphandlingen omfattar två delar: Bärgningstjänst; flytt av fordon till anvisad uppställningsplatsUppställningsplats; förvaring och skrotning av fordon. UM avser att teckna avtal med en leverantör per delområde, en leverantör kan dock bli aktuell för båda delområden. Anbudsgivaren kan därför lämna anbud på ett eller båda delområdena. I Växjö kommun är det Samhällsbyggnadsförvaltningen som ansvarar för flyttning av fordon. Beslut om flyttning grundas på lagen (SFS 1982:129) och förordningen (SFS 1982:198) om flyttning av fordon i vissa fall. Ett gott samarbete med ömsesidigt förtroende mellan beställare och leverantör är av stor vikt då det gäller hantering av annans egendom. Målet med avtalet är att uppnå en enkelhet i kommunikation och hantering, samt att helhetslösningen blir så kundanpassad som möjligt.

title: Switzerland – Structural shell work – Submission 211 Baumeister Anbau und Aufstockung AZB, Breitenbach
description: Gegenstand der Ausschreibung sind die Baumeisterarbeiten im Zusammenhang mit der geplanten Erweiterung und dem Umbau des bestehenden Alterszentrums Breitenbach. Der Leistungsumfang umfasst sämtliche für die Realisierung des Rohbaus erforderlichen Baumeisterarbeiten. Dazu gehören insbesondere die Baustelleneinrichtung, erforderliche Abbruch- und Rückbauarbeiten, Erd- und Aushubarbeiten, Kanalisations- und Entwässerungsarbeiten, Fundationen, Beton- und Stahlbetonarbeiten, Schalungs- und Bewehrungsarbeiten, Mauerwerksarbeiten sowie ergänzende Arbeiten am bestehenden Gebäude. Weiter sind die erforderlichen Durchbrüche, Aussparungen, Schlitze, Kernbohrungen und Anpassungsarbeiten im Bestand sowie das fachgerechte Schliessen von Öffnungen und Aussparungen Bestandteil der ausgeschriebenen Leistungen. Ebenfalls enthalten sind sämtliche notwendigen Nebenarbeiten, Transporte, Materialumschläge und Koordinationsleistungen gemäss den Ausschreibungsunterlagen. Ein wesentlicher Bestandteil des Auftrags sind die Anschlüsse zwischen dem bestehenden Gebäude und der Erweiterung. Die Arbeiten sind entsprechend den Projekt- und Ausführungsunterlagen sowie den geltenden Normen, Vorschriften und behördlichen Vorgaben auszuführen. Da das Alterszentrum während der Bauzeit weiterhin betrieben wird, sind die Arbeiten etappenweise und unter besonderer Berücksichtigung des laufenden Betriebs auszuführen. Zugänge, Flucht- und Rettungswege sowie die betrieblich notwendigen Erschliessungen sind jederzeit gemäss Bauablauf und Vorgaben der Bauleitung sicherzustellen. Die Ausführung erfordert eine enge terminliche und technische Koordination mit der Bauleitung sowie mit den übrigen am Bau beteiligten Unternehmern. Die Arbeiten sind gemäss Bauprogramm, Leistungsverzeichnis und den weiteren Bestandteilen der Ausschreibungsunterlagen auszuführen.
